title: Ravens put OL Hakeem Adeniji on reserve/retired list
summary: Hakeem Adeniji will not be providing the Ravens with offensive line depth this season.
full_text: Hakeem Adeniji will not be providing the Ravens with offensive line depth this season. The team announced on Monday morning that Adeniji has been placed on the reserve/retired list. Adeniji signed with the Ravens a little over a week ago, but he has decided against continuing his NFL career. Adeniji was a Bengals sixth-round pick in 2020 and he started 15 of the 39 regular season games he played over three years with the team. He also made seven starts in the postseason. Adeniji, who saw action at both guard and tackle, moved on to the Vikings in 2024 and the Cowboys in 2025. He played 16 games and made one start in those stops.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mike McCarthy wants Aaron Rodgers to play in first two preseason games
summary: The Steelers have a new head coach this season and they have a new plan for Aaron Rodgers in the preseason.
full_text: The Steelers have a new head coach this season and they have a new plan for Aaron Rodgers in the preseason. Rodgers did not play any preseason snaps in Mike Tomlin's final year as the head coach in Pittsburgh, but Mike McCarthy wants to see him in game action this August. Rodgers told Mike Silver of TheAthletic.com that McCarthy wants him to play in the team's first two preseason games. “He [wants me out there for] 30 or 40 plays ,” Rodgers said. “I said, ‘Mike, if you want me to play, I’ll play.’ I’m not saying I want to do it. But if he wants me to, I will.” In a stroke of scheduling kismet, the Steelers' first two preseason games are against the Packers and the Jets. Rodgers played two series for the Jets in the 2023 preseason, but his last extensive preseason action came in 2018 with the Packers. It appears that will change this summer.
author: Josh Alper

title: Commanders activate LB Kain Medrano
summary: Linebacker Kain Medrano is ready to get on the field at Commanders training camp.
full_text: Linebacker Kain Medrano is ready to get on the field at Commanders training camp. Medrano was placed on the physically unable to perform list to open camp, but the team announced that he has been activated on Monday morning. Medrano has been dealing with a hamstring injury. Medrano was a sixth-round pick last year and he appeared in nine games as a rookie. He had five tackles and a fumble recovery while playing exclusively on special teams. Washington still has cornerback Trey Amos, defensive end Dorance Armstrong, and defensive end Deatrich Wise on the PUP list. Punter Tress Way is on the non-football injury list.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ashton Jeanty: Expectation is for me to lead, so I have to make a big jump
summary: Ashton Jeanty came into the NFL with high expectations for what he'd do in the Raiders' backfield, but the 2025 first-round pick's rookie season did not meet them.
full_text: '' Ashton Jeanty came into the NFL with high expectations for what he'd do in the Raiders' backfield, but the 2025 first-round pick's rookie season did not meet them. Jeanty averaged 3.7 yards per carry while running behind a weak offensive line and the Raiders went 3-14 before firing Pete Carroll after one season as the team's head coach. Klint Kubiak replaced Carroll and the team invested in a pair of free agent additions to a line that has left tackle Kolton Miller back to full health, which raises hope that Jeanty will now be in position to thrive. While at training camp last week, Jeanty said that he's also working to make sure that he's a leader for the team rather than just being along for the ride. "Yeah, I think being more vocal for sure ," Jeanty said, via Jared Feinberg of SI.com. "I mean, it's always tough being in the first year trying to figure out so much stuff. But this year, there's a lot of expectations for me and I think I've got to make a big jump. I think that starts with helping my teammates as well and just being a better teammate. So, I think that starts with leadership." The Raiders had visions of success under Carroll at this point last year, so there's not much need for a reminder of how summer optimism can curdle come September. Jeanty making good on pre-draft prognostications would go a long way toward making sure that doesn't happen again this time.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ben Johnson: Luther Burden competes like Amon-Ra St. Brown, wants to be the best
summary: Bears coach Ben Johnson says wide receiver Luther Burden is poised to build off his promising rookie season in 2025 and become one of the best receivers in the NFL.
full_text: Bears coach Ben Johnson says wide receiver Luther Burden is poised to build off his promising rookie season in 2025 and become one of the best receivers in the NFL. Maybe the very best. Asked on Fox 32 in Chicago about saying Burden is destined to be one of the best wide receivers in the NFL, Johnson says he recognizes that Burden is among an elite group of players who are special in the way they compete. "They kind of flip a switch when they go on the field and they feel like they're invincible and they're the best players out there," Johnson said. Johnson was the Dolphins' wide receivers coach when Jarvis Landry was one of the NFL's best receivers in Miami, and more recently coached Amon-Ra St. Brown with the Lions. Johnson said both of those players are like Burden in the way they compete on every single down. "St. Brown in Detroit, who I have a strong affinity for, he plays the game the same way. I feel that from Luther," Johnson said. "He wasn't a full-time starter for us a year ago, but the snaps that he did have, he's got that competitive edge and desire to be great, and it's carried over into the spring and summer as well. He's been a regular in our building, working with our strength staff. He wants to be the most conditioned player on the team. wants to be one of the strongest receivers on the team and just continues to soak in all the knowledge." Last year Burden caught 47 passes as a rookie, finishing second among the Bears' wide receivers in receptions behind D.J. Moore. This year Moore has been traded away, and the plan is for Burden to get more passes thrown his way. Johnson thinks Burden is more than ready.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Jadeveon Clowney: Signing with the Texans was "a really easy decision"
summary: “I've grown up and learned the game a lot more since leaving,” Clowney said. “I feel like I can help the younger guys."
full_text: Jadeveon Clowney says he feels like he's back home after signing with the Texans. Clowney, who arrived in Houston as the first overall pick in the 2014 NFL draft but left in 2019 and has played for six different teams since, re-signed with the Texans on Sunday and said he believes Houston is the perfect place for him. “I felt like they got a good team and I can help contribute. It was a really easy decision ,” Clowney told the Houston Chronicle . “It wasn't about the money.” The Texans traded Clowney to the Seahawks in 2019 and he played one year in Seattle. He then played one year with the Titans, two with the Browns, one with the Ravens, one with the Panthers and one with the Cowboys. And now he's back where his NFL career began. “I've grown up and learned the game a lot more since leaving,” Clowney said. “I feel like I can help the younger guys. I've learned how to lead and what it takes to get to a Super Bowl. I feel like I can help this team.” Clowney has never played in a Super Bowl, but he thinks he can do it with the Texans, this season. “I just know this team is good enough to go, and I can help,” Clowney said. “We've got to get to work and stay locked in.” The 33-year-old Clowney is on the tail end of his career, but he had 8.5 sacks last season, and if he can make that kind of contribution to the pass rush in Houston, he can make an already good defense better.
author: Michael David Smith

title: After taking coaching job at Georgia Tech, DeAndre Hopkins says he isn't retired
summary: Yes, receiver DeAndre Hopkins has taken a coaching job at Georgia Tech.
full_text: '' Yes, receiver DeAndre Hopkins has taken a coaching job at Georgia Tech. No, he hasn't closed the door on playing in 2026. " I haven’t retired from the NFL ," Hopkins posted Saturday on Twitter, via Andy Backstrom of Yahoo Sports. "But if you're a WR and you want to be great, come to Georgia Tech football." Hopkins, 34, is keeping himself busy as he waits for another opportunity. "DeAndre is one of the greatest receivers of all time, but his value to our program goes far beyond that," Georgia Tech head coach Brent Key said in the statement announcing Hopkins's arrival. "He has an exceptional knowledge of what we're doing on offense due to his long relationship with [offensive coordinator] George Godsey and strong familiarity with the ACC, but, most importantly, he's a leader of men that I'm very excited for our players to be around, on and off the field." Hopkins, who spent time working with the Patriots' coaching staff early in camp, would prefer not to be around, if that means continuing to play. For now, opportunity hasn't knocked. Hopkins wants the league to know that, even as he works as a coach, he's ready to keep playing. A first-round pick in 2013, Hopkins spent seven seasons with the Texans and three with the Cardinals before splitting 2024 between the Titans and Chiefs. He played for the Ravens in 2025. He has 1,006 career catches, 13,295 receiving yards, and 85 touchdowns. And he's clearly interested in adding to those numbers during what would be a 14th NFL season.
author: Mike Florio

title: After lost rookie season, Bucs LB David Walker is turning heads again
summary: Last year, Buccaneers rookie linebacker David Walker was making a great impression.
full_text: Last year, Buccaneers rookie linebacker David Walker was making a great impression. But then, in the team's third training-camp practice, he suffered a torn ACL. This year, Walker is back. And he's back to making a great impression again. “He’s got his quickness and his speed back,” Bucs coach Todd Bowles said, via Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times. “So as a pass rusher, he’s looked very good as far as his movements and everything else. I was just excited to see him in pads last year [before the injury], so right now he looks very good . He’s looking fast.” Walker, a fourth-round pick, is ready to make the impact he didn't get a chance to make in 2025. “I just want to thank God,” Walker said, per Stroud. “The injury was big and the whole time I knew that He didn’t bring me this far to bring me this far. So I knew I had to attack rehab, I knew I had to do those things and I’m here. I’m back playing the game that I love. It’s exciting. It’s exciting.” The Bucs will get a better look at what he can do when he practices for the first time in pads, on Monday. “I think he can do almost everything,” Bowles said. “Height-wise, he’s probably the shortest of the bunch. Everybody forgets he’s 260-something. He plays with great leverage and power. I think he’s played both sides. He’s probably a good inside kicker as well getting off the ball and doing some things like that. So when he gets the pads on, we’ll figure it out.” ”I’m just taking it day by day," Walker said. "I’m not trying to look too far ahead. I’m not trying to look at whether I might be playing or not. I’m trying to do what I can do to compete." If he does what the Bucs think he can do, they'll go a long way toward boosting their pass rush. Having first-round rookie Reuben Bain Jr. won't hurt.
author: Mike Florio

title: Davante Adams on his 13th season: "This is dog years out there"
summary: At 33, Rams receiver Davante Adams is young by societal standards.
full_text: At 33, Rams receiver Davante Adams is young by societal standards. By NFL standards, he's not quite Methuselah — but he's getting there. Speaking with reporters on Sunday, Adams addressed the fact that he's not getting any younger as he enters his 13th NFL season. (Then again, who is?) “I battle with that sometimes, I do," Adams said. "I am the old man and I feel young because I can still go out there and do young man stuff, but then my body don't necessarily feel the same way it's done as it was back at Puka [Nacua's] age. "At the end of the day, what's 13 times seven? Because this is dog years out here. It’s a whole different ball game than living years. If I can continue to play at a high level, I'll deal with the other stuff whether it's talking about me being old or a little bit of extra pain. It's just a little extra work you have to do to come out of it.” He's still playing at a high level. Adams caught 14 touchdown passes to lead the league (for the third time) in 2025, despite missing three regular-season games. And even though it doesn't get discussed much, Adams surely has a little extra motivation from the fact that the Rams explored trading for receiver A.J. Brown, which would have resulted in Adams being traded yet again. For now, Adams is going nowhere. When his fourteenth season (times seven) rolls around, who knows where he will be? For now, he's a Ram — and that gives him the best chance he's had to add a Super Bowl ring to a potential Hall of Fame resume. Six-time Pro Bowler. Three-time first-team All-Pro. Seventh all-time in receiving touchdowns. Sixteenth in catches. Twenty-sixth in receiving yards. The longer he plays, the higher he'll climb.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cowboys sign OL Sebastian Gutierrez, waive LB Charles Snowden
summary: The Cowboys swapped out an injured defensive lineman for an offensive lineman on Sunday.
full_text: The Cowboys swapped out an injured defensive lineman for an offensive lineman on Sunday. The team announced the signing of Sebastian Gutierrez to their active roster. Defensive end Charles Snowden was waived with an injury designation to open a spot for Gutierrez in Dallas. Gutierrez was released by the Patriots last month. He spent part of the 2025 preseason with the Browns and was on New England's practice squad during the regular season. He has appeared in two regular season games since entering the league as an undrafted free agent in 2022. Snowden will revert to injured reserve if he goes unclaimed. He was previously suspended for the first three games of the regular season for a Personal Conduct Policy violation.
author: Josh Alper

title: 49ers sign RB Khalil Herbert, DL Titus Leo
summary: The 49ers made a handful of roster moves on Sunday.
full_text: '' The 49ers made a handful of roster moves on Sunday. They have signed running back Khalil Herbert and defensive lineman Titus Leo to their 90-man roster. Defensive lineman Mikail Kamara was waived with an injury designation and cornerback Eli Apple was released. Herbert ran 16 times for 52 yards in seven games for the Jets last season. The 2021 sixth-round pick spent his first three seasons with the Bears and split the 2024 season between Chicago and Cincinnati. Leo had four tackles in four games for the Patriots in 2024. He spent time on the Eagles' practice squad last season. The NFL's daily transaction report for Sunday shows that the Niners also hosted linebackers Andre Carter, Ogbo Okoronkwo, and Xavier Thomas for workouts.
author: Josh Alper

title: Myles Garrett out of practice with lower body soreness, but Sean McVay says Rams aren't worried
summary: Myles Garrett missed a third consecutive day of practice, but Rams coach Sean McVay said the defensive end has lower body soreness and nothing of concern.
full_text: Myles Garrett missed a third consecutive day of practice, but Rams coach Sean McVay said the defensive end has lower body soreness and nothing of concern. " Nothing to worry about , so we're erring on the side of being smart with him," McVay said, via video from the team. "Reggie [Scott, the team's senior director of sports medicine and performance] and those guys do such a great job, and he is as tough as it gets. So, we want to make sure that he feels as good as possible. As you know, guys that have played a lot of football, we've got a lot of opportunities to be able to get better, but we also want to make sure we're getting an understanding of how best to work with him. He's been outstanding, but there was a little bit of soreness. We said, 'Let's err on the side of caution.' Then, we'll see. He won't be on tomorrow either, and then we'll see what it looks like after the day off. I don't want to put the cart before the horse, but I would expect him to be ready to go in the next block." The Browns had an in-season practice plan for Garrett with built-in load management days off. It worked. Garrett played all 17 games each of the past two seasons and has missed only four games over the past six seasons. McVay reiterated the Rams are unconcerned about their prized offseason acquisition, a two-time Defensive Player of the Year. "We are erring on the side of caution," McVay said. "He's had checkups, all that kind of stuff, so there's nothing to worry about. It's more about how do we keep him as fresh as possible while getting the necessary callous, if you will, to feel as good as possible so that when we do play in Australia, he's ready to play and do his thing. "But there's no reason for concern, and I look forward to getting him back out there."
author: Charean Williams

title: Eight years later, Jadeveon Clowney returns to the Texans
summary: No. 1 overall pick in 2014 returns to the team that drafted him.
full_text: At a time when the signs were pointing to a potential return to Cleveland from pass rusher Jadeveon Clowney, he's instead returning to a different former team. NFL Network reports that Clowney has agreed to terms with the Texans. Clowney, who arrived in Houston as the first overall pick in the 2014 draft, spent five years there. He was a Pro Bowler in 2016, 2017, and 2018. After his fifth season, Clowney was traded to the Seahawks. A year later, Clowney joined the Titans. After two seasons in Cleveland, Clowney's game of NFL hopscotch continued in Baltimore, Carolina, and Dallas. He had 8.5 sacks in 13 games (six starts) for the Cowboys in 2025. Clowney joins a defense that is already chock full of superstars. With Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter as the starters, Clowney gives them a robust rotation that can wear an offensive line down, and that can wear a quarterback out. Watch the Texans this year. Their defense will continue to be dominant. And their offense needs to simply be competent to provide enough balance to make it to the AFC Championship for the first time and, in turn, to the Super Bowl for the first time.
author: Mike Florio

title: Saints put WR Ja'Lynn Polk on reserve/retired list
summary: Wide receiver Ja'Lynn Polk is walking away from football ahead of his third NFL season.
full_text: Wide receiver Ja'Lynn Polk is walking away from football ahead of his third NFL season. The Saints announced that they placed Polk on the reserve/retired list on Sunday. Polk entered the league as a 2024 second-round pick in New England and played 15 games for the team during his rookie season. He had 12 catches for 87 yards and two touchdowns. The Patriots traded Polk and a seventh-round pick to the Saints last September for a sixth-round pick. Polk did not appear in any games due to a shoulder injury and Sunday's move means that he won't be playing in any games for the NFC South team in the future either.
author: Josh Alper

title: Steelers sign S Rayshawn Jenkins, cut Darnell Savage
summary: The Steelers signed safety Rayshawn Jenkins to a one-year contract, the team announced Sunday.
full_text: The Steelers signed safety Rayshawn Jenkins to a one-year contract, the team announced Sunday. In a corresponding move, the Steelers released safety Darnell Savage. They signed Savage on June 2. He played two games for Jacksonville, eight for Washington and two for the Bills in 2025. Savage also started 13 games for the Jaguars in 2024 and spent five seasons with the Packers to begin his career. Jenkins entered the NFL as a fourth-round pick of the Chargers in 2017. He has spent time with the Chargers (2017-20), Jaguars (2021-23), Seahawks (2024) and Browns (2025). In 17 games with the Browns last season, Jenkins had 45 tackles, 19 of them solos, one interception, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery. He has appeared in 139 career games, starting 92. Jenkins has recorded 562 tackles, 5.5 sacks, two forced fumbles, 34 passes defensed, 11 interceptions and 20 tackles for a loss.
author: Charean Williams

title: Titans sign defensive tackles Khalen Saunders, Laki Tasi
summary: The Titans have two new defensive tackles in camp.
full_text: The Titans have two new defensive tackles in camp. The team announced the signings of Khalen Saunders and Laki Tasi on Sunday afternoon. They also confirmed the previously reported signing of defensive back Derrick Canteen. Saunders played for the Jets and Jaguars in 2025. He had 12 tackles and a sack in nine games for the two AFC teams. The 2019 third-round pick has also played for the Chiefs and Saints. Tasi grew up as a rugby player in Australia and spent time on the Raiders' practice squad last season. He is exempt from the 90-man roster limit as an international player. The Titans waived safety Hudson Clark, defensive lineman David Ebuka Agoha, and defensive lineman Cam Horsley in corresponding moves.
author: Josh Alper

title: Commanders sign C Trey Hill
summary: The Commanders announced a pair of roster moves on Sunday afternoon.
full_text: The Commanders announced a pair of roster moves on Sunday afternoon. They have signed center Trey Hill to the active roster. Cornerback Tre Hawkins was waived in a corresponding move. Hill was a Bengals sixth-round pick in 2021 and he remained with the team through the 2024 season. He spent time with the Packers and Bears last season, but did not appear in any games. He was also on the Titans' roster for most of the offseason. Hill appeared in 25 games for the Bengals and made three starts. Hawkins played in one game for Washington last season and 20 games for the Giants over his first two NFL seasons.
author: Josh Alper

title: Reports: Texans to sign DL Mario Edwards, LB Sione Takitaki
summary: The Texans are bringing back defensive lineman Mario Edwards.
full_text: The Texans are bringing back defensive lineman Mario Edwards. Edwards was released in March, but Jonathan Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports that the team is signing him after a visit this weekend. Edwards had 13 tackles and 1.5 sacks in 14 games for the Texans last season, but missed the rest of the year with a torn pectoral. He also appeared in 13 games and made 12 starts for Houston in 2024. Aaron Wilson of KPRC reports that the Texans will be signing linebacker Sione Takitaki as well. Takitaki worked out for the team on Friday and will help fill in for Jake Hansen, who is out for an indefinite period with an ankle injury. Takitaki played in three games for the Vikings last year. He has also appeared in 83 games for the Browns and Patriots. UPDATE 4:03 p.m. ET : The Texans announced the Edwards signing. They have waived running back Evan Hull and offensive tackle Derrick Graham.
author: Josh Alper

title: Who are the potential successors to Roger Goodell?
summary: This week, Roger Goodell will be in Canton for the annual distribution of a fresh set of gold jackets.
full_text: This week, Roger Goodell will be in Canton for the annual distribution of a fresh set of gold jackets. (He'll eventually get one, too, given that his two predecessors — Pete Rozelle and Paul Tagliabue — are in the Hall of Fame.) As to Goodell, the more important word than "predecessor" is "successor." With a new contract expected to eventually supplant a deal that expires in March 2027, the question is lingering as to who will take the wheel when Goodell's autograph exits The Duke. In an item for Front Office Sports , Mark Maske (formerly of the Washington Post ) listed 11 potential candidates for the job : PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp, NFL executive V.P. of club business, major events, and international Peter O'Reilly; NFL general counsel Ted Ullyot; NFL management council general counsel Larry Ferazini; NFL CFO Christine Dorfler; NFL chief revenue officer Renie Anderson; NFL executive V.P. of media distribution Hans Schroeder; Bears president and CEO Kevin Warren; Rams president Kevin Demoff; SoFi CEO Anthony Noto; and NBA Commissioner Adam Silver. My immediate thought based on the list was "none of the above," mainly because I personally believe Goodell, 67, will stay until the current candidates will likely be too old to step into a job that has seen only two transitions since Rozelle was hired in 1960. Given the long tenures of the last three Commissioners, the owners presumably will want to find someone who will be good enough to do the job well, and young enough to do the job for a long time. But if, say, Goodell and the owners reach an impasse in their negotiations and he leaves, Maske's list provides a potential starting point. Based on our own poking around, Rolapp, O'Reilly, and Dorfler would be the most likely candidates from Maske's 11. Anderson would be a serious candidate, too, if she truly wanted the job and everything that goes along with it. Demoff and Noto would be possibilities. Noto, as we hear it, may have to unruffle feathers tracing to what some perceive as a less-than-graceful exit from 345 (which was 280 at the time). Here are a couple of others to watch, who weren't on Maske's list: NFL Media senior V.P. David Jurenka and Endeavor/TKO president Mark Shapiro. Also, it would not be Adam Silver. "Never" is the word that was used. Also, "zero-point-zero chance." As Maske notes, one potential outcome would be to hire a CEO who would run the entire business and a football czar who would report to the CEO. Years ago, we heard that the ongoing growth of the NFL may require that; the late Jim Irsay was the first owner to speak publicly about that possibility. That's an issue for down the road, if Goodell hangs around beyond his current deal and, possibly if not likely, the next one and, possibly, the next one. He could do the job until his 80th birthday, if he wanted and if his health permits it. He could possibly do it into his 80s. (At this point in his life, what else would he do?) Frankly, the biggest takeaway from Maske's snapshot of candidates is that there isn't an obvious short list of can't-miss replacements. Which gives Goodell a little more leverage in the ongoing talks — especially with most of the broadcast deals expiring in 2030 and the Collective Bargaining Agreement terminating in 2031.
author: Mike Florio

title: Travis Hunter says he wants to play every snap after putting on a show in practice
summary: Travis Hunter played 324 offensive snaps and 162 defensive snaps in seven appearances last season before his knee injury.
full_text: Travis Hunter played 324 offensive snaps and 162 defensive snaps in seven appearances last season before his knee injury. The Jaguars wide receiver/cornerback is expected to play more on defense than offense, and that has been the case thus far in training camp. He flashed on both sides in Sunday's practice, with an interception and two catches, including a 35-yarder. Hunter took 10 snaps on defense and seven on offense in team work, according to Michael DiRocco of ESPN, and has taken 34 snaps on defense and 22 on offense in 11-on-11 work so far through a week of camp. Hunter told Judy Battista of NFL Network that he wants to play every snap on both sides, something his former college coach, Deion Sanders, said Hunter is capable of doing . “ All of them ," Hunter said when asked how many snaps he wants to play. "I can’t stay on the sideline." In winning the Heisman Trophy at Colorado in 2024, Hunter played 688 defensive snaps and 672 on offense. It prompted the Jaguars to trade up to second overall to draft him. Trevor Lawrence said he isn't lobbying for more snaps for Hunter. “He's lobbying enough on his own. He'd play every snap on both sides of the ball if he was able to,” the quarterback told Battista. “He's so talented, and I know that no matter where he's playing, he's going to help our team. On offense, on defense. So where does he help us the most? I'll let the coaches make that decision. I know when he's on offense, he's making plays. I also know that we have so many good skill players on offense that, even when he's not over there, we're able to be explosive and find these plays. Look at our room, with [Brian Thomas], Jakobi [Meyers], Parker [Washington], some of the young guys we brought in. Then our tight end room is just really, really versatile and good. So we have so many threats, and I'll let our coaches kind of figure that out.” Hunter tore the lateral collateral ligament in his right knee during an Oct. 30 practice. He underwent surgery on Nov. 11. He finished his rookie season with 28 catches for 298 yards and a touchdown on offense and 15 tackles on defense.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jameson Williams: No question Jahmyr Gibbs should be the highest-paid RB in the NFL
summary: Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams was asked today whether Jahmyr Gibbs deserves to be the highest-paid running back in the NFL.
full_text: Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams was asked today whether Jahmyr Gibbs deserves to be the highest-paid running back in the NFL. He said that's an easy question to answer. "Of course. No question. He's the best. I wouldn't even say look at the stats, look at the film. Nobody close. He's the best," Williams said. Williams said he's not just a friend of Gibbs, but a fan of Gibbs. "When Zero gets on the field, it's game changing for us. To me he's unstoppable. He gets through the line of scrimmage, he goes 70. I love playing with him. I love watching him. He's got one of the best games I've ever seen," Williams said. Williams said he's eager to see Gibbs back on the field. "He's the best of the best. Hopefully coming up we get to see my boy get something done so he can be back out here for us," Williams said. "I'm really excited for him. I know what he can do for us." Gibbs is in attendance at training camp but not practicing while he negotiates a new contract.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Sam Ehlinger pushing Jarrett Stidham for Broncos' backup job
summary: Sam Ehlinger took the Broncos' second-team snaps on Saturday, Mike Klis of 9News reports.
full_text: Sam Ehlinger took the Broncos’ second-team snaps on Saturday, Mike Klis of 9News reports. Jarrett Stidham, the team's backup to Bo Nix the past two seasons, was with the third team. “There was nothing remarkable or anything that we discussed in a meeting, so maybe they just unfolded where . . . I wouldn’t make anything into it,’’ Broncos head coach Sean Payton said, via Klis. It was the first time Ehlinger has run the No. 2 offense, though, when Nix is healthy. (Ehlinger was the backup to Stidham in the AFC Championship Game when Nix was out with an ankle injury.) Ehlinger had a chance to leave for Washington and Indianapolis last season — and perhaps a better chance at the No. 2 job — but remained on the Broncos' practice squad. Now, it appears he will push Stidham for the backup job. “I think we just sold our program and the offense,’’ Payton said of keeping Ehlinger. “We could never promise anything other than [a chance to develop]. I would say this, we saw immediate growth, and I think you’d have to ask him, but I think he felt like, ‘I want to continue with this offense and continue where I’m going.’ I think he felt good about it to make that decision.”
author: Charean Williams

title: James Robinson gets a tryout with Raiders
summary: Six years after running back James Robinson rushed for 1,070 yards as a rookie in 2020 with the Jaguars, he's looking for a path back to the NFL.
full_text: '' Six years after running back James Robinson rushed for 1,070 yards as a rookie in 2020 with the Jaguars, he's looking for a path back to the NFL. Robinson had a tryout on Saturday with the Raiders. He played most recently for the Louisville Kings of the UFL, rushing for 324 yards in six regular-season games and adding 128 in two postseason games for the eventual league champions. Robinson was traded to the Jets during his third season, to the Jets. He spent 2023 with the Packers, appearing in only one game and having just one carry. He did not play in the NFL in 2024 or 2025. For his NFL career, Robinson has rushed for 2,264 yards. (So far.) Also trying out on Saturday were running backs Dare Ogunbawale and Kenny McIntosh. Ogunbawale, a nine-year veteran, spent the last four seasons in Houston. His tenure including kicking a 29-yard field goal in a 2023 win over Tampa Bay, 39-37, after Texans kicker Ka'imi Fairbarn suffered a quad injury. McIntosh, a seventh-round pick of the Seahawks in 2024, was released on July 27.
author: Mike Florio

title: Titans to sign DB Derrick Canteen
summary: The Titans have agreed to terms with defensive back Derrick Canteen, Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reports.
full_text: ''' The Titans have agreed to terms with defensive back Derrick Canteen, Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reports. Earlier Sunday, the Titans announced the signing of cornerback Mario Goodrich, cutting defensive back Jeadyn Lukus in a corresponding move. Canteen, 25, reunites with Robert Saleh on the Titans. The two were together in San Francisco last season. The 49ers cut Canteen last week. He played collegiately at Georgia Southern from 2019-22, Virginia Tech in 2023 and Cincinnati in 2025. Canteen signed with the 49ers after going undrafted last year. He made the roster out of training camp but was cut a week later and re-signed to the practice squad. Canteen, who did not see any regular-season action in 2025, signed a futures contract with the 49ers after the season.
author: Charean Williams

title: Packers T Zach Tom changes last name to Bako-Bewele
summary: The Packers are expected to have the same starting right tackle as last season when they take the field in September, but there will be a different name on the back of his jersey.
full_text: The Packers are expected to have the same starting right tackle as last season when they take the field in September, but there will be a different name on the back of his jersey. Zach Tom told reporters on Sunday that he has changed his last name to Bako-Bewele. The name is a combination of names from his grandparents and the tackle explained that he wanted to honor his family's Nigerian heritage. "That’s really the main reason why I did it," Bako-Bewele said, via Matt Schneidman of TheAthletic.com. "I want to have a name, especially when I start having kids, I want to have a name that I can pass down where it represents where they came from, where I came from. I just feel like that name — people will see that name and have a good understanding of who I am, where I come from." Bako-Bewele is going into his fifth season with the Packers and he signed a four-year extension before the 2025 campaign.
author: Josh Alper

title: Saints defensive tackle Bryan Bresee to have surgery for torn ACL
summary: Saints defensive tackle Bryan Bresee's knee injury didn't look good when it happened, and now it's confirmed that he needs surgery to repair a torn ACL.
full_text: Saints defensive tackle Bryan Bresee's knee injury didn’t look good when it happened, and now it's confirmed that he needs surgery to repair a torn ACL. New Orleans head coach Kellen Moore confirmed today what was feared about Bresee's injury. "He's gonna have surgery," Moore said. Bresee suffered the injury in practice on Wednesday. His absence will be a big loss for the Saints, who drafted him in the first round in 2023 and picked up his fifth-year option this year. Bresee will now get ready for the 2027 season, when he has a guaranteed salary of $13.9 million.

title: Vikings sign CB Jarod Washington
summary: The Vikings announced a couple of roster moves on Sunday.
full_text: The Vikings announced a couple of roster moves on Sunday. They have signed cornerback Jarod Washington. Running back Kejon Owens was waived to create room for Washington on their 90-man roster. Washington went undrafted out of South Carolina State earlier this year. He attended rookie minicamps for the Chiefs and Buccaneers, but did not sign with either club. Washington had 33 tackles, a tackle for loss, two interceptions, 22 passes defensed and a forced fumble last season. Owens signed with Minnesota after going undrafted out of FIU. He was placed on the non-football illness list at the start of training camp.

title: Jaxson Dart on John Harbaugh: We're all buying in because of how great a coach he is
summary: Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart says he and his teammates are lining up behind new head coach John Harbaugh.
full_text: '' Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart says he and his teammates are lining up behind new head coach John Harbaugh. Asked about Harbaugh on NFL Network , Dart identified one thing that makes him special as a coach: "His leadership." "The way that he carries himself as an individual, a man, it's something you can really, really respect, day in and day out," Dart continued. "The biggest thing is, he's never trying to change anybody from who they are, but he's putting out his culture, his plan, and it's for us to buy into it. That's really cool to have, when you have all these different guys coming in to a brand new system, who have different experiences, some of us being younger, a lot of the vets, but we're all buying into the exact same plan because we trust him, because of how great of a coach he is and the man he is as well." The Giants have struggled to find coaching stability since the departure of Tom Coughlin, going from Ben McAdoo to Pat Shurmur to Joe Judge to Brian Daboll. Dart thinks they've brought in the right guy in Harbaugh.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Matt LaFleur: Tucker Kraft could participate in joint practice with Cardinals
summary: Packers tight end Tucker Kraft was able to ride a bike to the practice field — and to practice on it — on Friday, his first work since suffering a torn ACL on November 2.
full_text: Packers tight end Tucker Kraft was able to ride a bike to the practice field — and to practice on it — on Friday, his first work since suffering a torn ACL on November 2. With the primary goal having him ready to go for Week 1, Kraft could be back in the mix when the Packers engage in a joint practice with the Cardinals on August 26. Coach Matt LaFleur said it's a realistic target. "I mean, he's got to hit all the benchmarks along the way, and if that's the case, then absolutely," LaFleur told reporters on Sunday. So far, LaFleur is happy with what he has seen from the third-round pick in the 2023 draft. "I think we're obviously taking it slow with him because he's such an important player to us," LaFleur said. "But, yeah, I think he handled everything great." Kraft is in the last year of a rookie deal that pays him $3.6 million in 2026. He has said he has no qualms about practicing without the long-term security he has earned. And while LaFleur praised Kraft for doing so, here's the inescapable reality — if Kraft gets injured again, he won't get the kind of multi-year deal he'd prefer to receive. At that point, the Packers would press the brakes, possibly with a one-year deal for 2027, until Kraft would be able to demonstrate that he's back to form. Of course, Kraft may feel compelled to do that now, given his 2025 knee injury. Which requires Kraft to take a calculated risk aimed at securing his reward. Ideally for Kraft, he'll get it before Week 1.
author: Mike Florio

title: 911 call reveals frantic effort to revive Aldon Smith
summary: Former NFL defensive end Aldon Smith died suddenly on June 13.
full_text: ' Former NFL defensive end Aldon Smith died suddenly on June 13. The situation prompted former teammate Donte Whitner to express concern about what had happened. An important piece in the potentially complicated puzzle emerged on Friday, when the San Francisco Chronicle published the six-minute 911 call that was made after Smith was found unresponsive. "Come on!" former 49ers teammate Anthony Dixon says on the call. "He's not responding! . . . Oh my God, Aldon, brother!" (Whitner had identified former 49ers teammate Anthony Davis as someone who was present when Smith died. Whitner apparently was referring to Anthony Dixon.) "I have a friend, it looks like he fainted or passed away in my car," Amir Shirazi, who previously spoke to the Chronicle about Smith's passing, said to the dispatcher. "He just had pizza and I came back and he was just fainted and passed out in the car." The dispatcher asked if Smith was awake. "No, it looks like he passed away," Shirazi said. "I hope to God not. But he's not breathing, no." Shirazi also was asked whether he had access to a defibrillator. He said he didn't. "My friend is trying to wake him up," Shirazi told the dispatcher. "He won't wake up." Shirazi provided more information to the Chronicle via text message on Friday: "He was a healthy young man in my opinion and completely normal in my eyes the whole morning when I was with him. . . . [He] didn't complain about nothing to me in the car and he was relaxed, finished eating some pizza and drinking a water bottle right before. Hopefully the autopsy comes out soon." Smith's cause of death remains undisclosed, if it's even known. In the days after Smith's passing, his family hired lawyers to investigate the circumstances surrounding his death.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFL training camp QB battles: Breaking down four competitions, plus veterans that need to watch their backs
summary: Training camp has brought several quarterback competitions into focus, with Week 1 roles still unsettled around the league
full_text:
When it comes to training camp storylines, quarterback battles take center stage. This summer, we have a handful of battles to sink our teeth into, ranging from Atlanta, Minnesota, Cleveland and Las Vegas. On top of those battles, there are also a few signal callers in precarious positions. Their jobs are necessarily at risk, but they have plenty to prove to put themselves on a stronger footing.
Below, we take the temperature of the four quarterback battles currently underway, highlighting the latest updates from camp, plus give our prediction of who we see coming out on top. Then, we'll put the spotlight on a handful of veteran quarterbacks who aren't in a battle, but need to watch their backs.
Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy are entrenched in a head-to-head competition for the Week 1 job in Minnesota. To begin camp, Kevin O'Connell split the reps between the two signal-callers, but Murray does appear to be gaining momentum as of late. Murray showcased his best practice of camp on Saturday, according to a wide array of reports at Vikings camp, including ESPN's Kevin Seifert . Most importantly, he was on the field for 16 of the first team offense's 22 snaps on 11-on-11 drills, per Seifert. He also completed all three of his passes to Justin Jefferson during the session, which is a key rapport metric to monitor. As for McCarthy, who did get more snaps over Murray during Friday's session (32 vs. 26 in full-offense drills), didn't have as successful a practice on Saturday as Murray.
While that's the up-close view of this battle, at a more macro level, it's hard not to see Murray coming out on top. McCarthy is coming off a 2025 season, his first as the full-time starter, where he struggled mightily. He went 6-4 over his 10 starts and completed 57.6% of his passes, averaged 163.2 passing yards per game, and registered 11 touchdowns with 12 interceptions. His 72.6 passer rating ranked last among qualified quarterbacks. While McCarthy did seem to find his footing down the stretch (4-0 record with a 100.4 passer rating), that didn't stop Minnesota from signing Murray as a free agent. While Murray has a shaky injury history (has missed 30 of a possible 68 games over the last five seasons), his talent provides a much higher upside for O'Connell's offense.
Prediction : Kyler Murray wins the Week 1 job.
The Falcons technically have a quarterback battle on their hands between Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr,, but it hasn't exactly been a slugfest. Why? Well, injuries have gotten in the way of this being a true competition. Of course, the most notable injury surrounds Penix, who is still rehabbing from a torn ACL he suffered in Week 11 last season. New coach Kevin Stefanski said last week that Penix is still not cleared for full team activities , which means he cannot take part in 11-on-11 drills. Penix also provided an update to reporters, and the timeline isn't encouraging for his chances to secure the Week 1 gig. He noted that it could be another four weeks before reaching the next stage of his rehabilitation. If you tack that into the calendar, Penix is looking at being cleared by the end of August, meaning he'd likely miss all of the preseason. Under that scenario, it's hard to imagine him truly pushing Tagovailoa.
Speaking of Tagovailoa, he also was not on the field last week due to a reported back injury. Stefanski described the injury as minor and the former Dolphins quarterback "will be out there sooner rather than later." Under different circumstances with a healthy Penix, this could've been a pocket for Tagovailoa to lose some ground. Instead, it won't really move the needle.
Prediction : Tua Tagovailoa wins the Week 1 job.
In Cleveland, first-year coach Todd Monken is mulling whether to name Deshaun Watson or Shedeur Sanders the starter for the Browns in 2026. Through the early days of camp, it doesn't appear as though either quarterback has truly endeared himself. Watson has thrown multiple interceptions in two of the four practice days, according to The Athletic . Despite that, Monken tipped his hand in favor of Sanders, continuing to split the reps between the two with the first-team offense.
As a rookie, Sanders went 3-4 for the Browns, and the passing metrics leave little to be desired. For the season, he completed 57% of his passes, threw seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions, and posted a 68.1 passer rating. Since his debut in Week 11, Sanders threw an NFL-high 10 picks. That said, Sanders has noted this summer that he feels much more comfortable heading into his second season, so that could help level out those numbers amid this battle with Watson.
As for Watson, he hasn't played since tearing his Achilles in Week 7 of the 2024 season. He also suffered another tear in that same Achilles tendon during his rehab, which resulted in him missing the entire 2025 season. In all, he's played in just 19 games over the last four seasons since coming over to the Browns in that blockbuster trade with the Texans . While he's shown plenty of rust over the course of camp thus far, it does seem like Monken is giving him the space to shake it off and, at times, feels like he has the inside track at the job.
Prediction : Deshaun Watson wins the Week 1 job.
As we look to Las Vegas, it's less of a quarterback competition and more of a philosophical approach with how the Raiders want to handle the development of Fernando Mendoza , who they selected with the No. 1 overall pick at the 2026 NFL Draft . Klint Kubiak has stated that he believes the best way to usher a young quarterback into the NFL is to bring him along slowly and not start him in the game. The ideal approach is to have an established veteran begin the year and then eventually hand the keys over to him when he's ready.
The Raiders have an established veteran on the roster in Kirk Cousins , and he's been the top quarterback throughout the offseason. That includes Kubiak putting Cousins out there as QB1 on the first day of training camp to work with the first-team offense. Even if Mendoza takes training camp by storm, Kubiak's path for the young quarterback could lead to him starting his career as Cousins' backup. That said, it's only a matter of time before the Mendoza era begins in Sin City.
Prediction : Kirk Cousins wins the Week 1 job.
Mayfield isn't in danger of losing his starting job, but his future with the Buccaneers beyond 2026 is murky at best. The veteran enters the final year of his contract and, after the two sides were unable to come to terms on an extension by his self-imposed deadline, negotiations are over. Now, Mayfield is focusing on the upcoming season, which could very well be his last in Tampa, especially after he acknowledged publicly that he felt "disrespected" by the organization.
This adds another layer of pressure for Mayfield, who is looking to rebound after his worst statistical season since becoming the Bucs starter. The 31-year-old is not only now tasked with bringing the Buccaneers back to the playoffs after an 8-9 campaign in 2025 snapped their streak of five-straight postseason appearances, but he's also again forced to prove his worth for a new contract (either with the Bucs or some other team as he eyes free agency in 2027).
After sitting out for the bulk of the offseason program as he sought a revised contract, the Cardinals agreed on a reworked deal with Brissett that will pay him up to $21 million in 2026, including $15.5 million guaranteed. While Brissett got his desired contract, it doesn't guarantee that he'll start the entire season for Arizona. The veteran will almost certainly be the Cardinals' QB1 to begin the 2026 campaign, but the franchise does have rookie Carson Beck waiting in the wings. The club selected the Miami quarterback in the third round of the draft this offseason, and will likely want to see what they have in him at some point. That's especially true if the season goes awry and they are in line for a top pick at the 2027 NFL Draft. Before…
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Can Patriots repeat? Drake Maye, Mike Vrabel face tougher 2026 road after stunning Super Bowl run
summary: After one of the greatest turnarounds in NFL history, the Patriots enter 2026 with higher expectations, a tougher schedule and major questions to answer
full_text:
The New England Patriots turned the tide in 2025. After three straight seasons of under .500 ball and two consecutive 4-13 campaigns, the Patriots catapulted into Super Bowl contention. With Drake Maye entering his second season and under new coach Mike Vrabel, the organization went 14-3 in the regular season and advanced to Super Bowl LX. While they were unable to hoist the Lombardi Trophy, falling to the Seattle Seahawks , it was still a historic turnaround for the franchise.
In fact, their 17-4 record (including playoffs) is the largest year-over-year win increase in NFL history (+13). They were also the first team ever to reach the Super Bowl following a 13-plus loss season. Helping spearhead that resurrection, Vrabel won Coach of the Year, while Maye finished second in MVP voting.
That Super Bowl run a season ago has not only put the Patriots back on the map but also raised the bar for what the region and the NFL expected of them heading into 2026. Labeled as one of the true contenders throughout the league, they won't catch teams sleeping as they may have in 2025, and the road ahead is far more treacherous.
Below, we'll comb through New England's upcoming schedule in 2026, highlight their key offseason additions and departures, and also highlight what they'll need to overcome to continue this ascent.
vs. Detroit Lions (Munich)
On paper, the 2026 Patriots are much more talented than the 2025 Patriots. They added some major weapons like A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs , bolstered the offensive line, and added some key pieces to the defense as well. While this version of New England may be better than last year's, its record may not be.
One of the biggest critiques of the Patriots from 2025 was that they stacked up a ton of wins because of an easy schedule. In the regular season, New England had the easiest strength of schedule since the 1999 Rams . As we look forward to this coming season, the road will not be as kind.
From the jump, the Patriots will be tested to a historic degree. They have the hardest strength of schedule from Week 1 through Week 4 (.721 opponent win percentage in 2025) in the last 40 years (1986 Eagles ). Three of those four games also take place on the road, adding another layer of difficulty. They are the first team since the 2019 Dolphins to open the season with three straight division winners. For reference, New England faced two division winners all of last season.
Beyond that grueling first month, New England enters the season with the sixth-hardest strength of schedule overall, and the AFC should be much more competitive this time around. Joe Burrow missed a chunk of the season due to injury, eliminating the Bengals as a contender, while Lamar Jackson and the Ravens and Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs also experienced down years. Provided those quarterbacks stay healthy, they should be among the top rivals to New England as they jockey for playoff positioning, along with their division rival in the Buffalo Bills.
So, if the Patriots succeed anywhere close to the level they reached in 2025, detractors won't have the easy-schedule narrative to lean on.
via DraftKings Sportsbook.
Currently, the biggest story surrounding the Patriots as they go through the initial days of training camp is that All-Pro cornerback Christian Gonzalez is still without a contract extension.
Earlier in camp, owner Robert Kraft told a group of reporters in Foxborough that the team had offered a contract that would make Gonzalez, who is under team control through 2027 (fifth-year option), the highest-paid corner in the NFL and the highest-paid player in franchise history. Despite that, pen has not been put to paper on a new deal. Unlike Kraft, Gonzalez chose not to discuss the negotiations publicly when asked about them at camp.
This is puzzling on a couple of different fronts. When it comes to Kraft saying they've offered him a market-setting extension, there might be some nuance there. The two sides aren't close to an agreement at the moment, Albert Breer of the MMQB told NBC Sports Boston just a few days ago. So, while an offer may have been extended to Gonzalez, it may not be to the caliber of the corner's liking, especially with the Seattle Seahawks and fellow defensive back Devon Witherspoon also narrowing in on a market-altering extension. Maybe Gonzalez and company are waiting for that deal to go down in hopes of boosting his value even higher?
Gonzalez has been taking part in New England's offseason program and has been on the field throughout training camp, neglecting to enact a hold-in, as many other players seeking a new contract do nowadays. In fact, he's basically done the opposite. Gonzalez was on the field as a full participant during the team's first day of padded practices, which was eye-opening. Typically, players would draw the line at participating in full-padded practices to avoid an injury becoming a sticking point in negotiations, but Gonzalez is going through the workouts in good faith.
Even though it hasn't become a speed bump in terms of the Patriots' on-field preparations for the 2026 season, getting Gonzalez done sooner rather than later is paramount.
Drake Maye was walloped in the playoffs. Throughout the postseason, Maye was sacked 21 times, which is the most in a single playoff run all-time. That constant pressure led to the MVP runner-up struggling mightily, and it all came to a head in Super Bowl LX, where Maye became the first player with three-plus turnovers in the second half of a Super Bowl since Rich Gannon in 2002. A key reason for Maye being under so much duress was poor play along the offensive line, particularly at left tackle with then-rookie Will Campbell .
Despite his struggles, the Patriots are sticking with their former No. 4 overall pick at left tackle. That said, the franchise did put resources towards bolstering the line this offseason. In free agency, they added Alijah Vera-Tucker by inking him to a three-year, $42 million contract. He'll slot in at left guard, and Jared Wilson will kick in to his natural center position after trading Garrett Bradbury to the Chicago Bears.
New England still has Morgan Moses at right tackle and Mike Onwenu at right guard, but did use the 28th overall pick at the 2026 NFL Draft to bring in tackle Caleb Lomu . The 6-foot-6, 313-pounder played left tackle at Utah, so he could be a failsafe option if Campbell's struggles continue. That said, he's been eyed by the team as the future at right tackle, given that Moses is entering his age-35 season.
Outside of getting Gonzalez's extension done, the biggest concern for the Patriots defense is the lack of top-tier talent and depth off the edge. This offseason, New England saw edge rusher K'Lavon Chaisson sign with the Commanders . Chaisson was second on the team with 7.5 sacks over the regular season, and was tied for the team lead in sacks over the playoffs (3).
Meanwhile, Harold Landry , who led the team in sacks last season, has opened camp on the PUP list as he continues to deal with a knee injury he suffered last season.
The team did add to the position group, signing veteran Dre'Mont Jones to a three-year, $39.5 million contract in free agency. Between the Ravens and Titans last season, Jones had seven total sacks and 24 quarterback hits, which were both career highs. They also drafted Gabe Jacas in the second round out of Illinois, but the pass rusher was just recently activated off the non-football injury list following a cleanup procedure on his knee after the draft.
With Landry's availability in question, New England is counting on Jones and/or Jacas to contribute in a big way out of the gate.
The most scandalous story surrounding the Patriots' offseason centered around their head coach, Mike Vrabel. The 2026 Coach of the Year was photographed at a Sedona resort with former NFL reporter for The Athletic, Dianna Russini. The two, who are married to different people, were pictured in a hot tub together and interlocking…
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Former No. 1 pick Jadeveon Clowney heading back to Texans for second stint: 'It was a no-brainer for me'
summary: Clowney is back with the Texans after closing last season with a career-best three-sack game
full_text:
It's never too late to come home, something three-time Pro Bowl edge rusher Jadeveon Clowney just found out.
The 2014 NFL Draft's first overall pick is returning to the Houston Texans after agreeing to terms on a contract, according to ESPN . Clowney concluded his 2025 season with the Dallas Cowboys with a bang, racking up a single-game career-high three sacks in Week 18 against New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart . Despite not suiting up for the Cowboys until Week 4, he finished with 8.5 sacks, his most in a season since producing 9.5 in 2023 with the Ravens . That figure also led Dallas in 2025.
"It's great," Clowney said in a phone interview with KPRC 2 in Houston . "It was a family decision. It wasn't about the money it was about chasing my legacy and chasing a Super bowl . I've got a lot of game left and want to contribute."
Now, there's a chance the former first-overall pick could play even better in 2026 at 33-years-old after going through training camp with the Texans alongside Houston's All-Pro edge rusher duo of Will Anderson Jr . and Danielle Hunter .
Anderson's 12 sacks tied for the eighth-most in the league in 2025 while ranking third in the NFL in quarterback pressures with 93. Anderson's 21% quarterback pressure rate led the league in 2025 among those with at least 300 pass rushes, per CBS Sports Research. That all added up to Anderson's first first-team All-Pro selection in his three-season career, in addition to being extended on a three-year, $150 million deal this offseason. His $50 million average per year salary makes him the highest-paid non-quarterback in the league. Hunter's 15.0 sacks in 2025 ranked as the third-most in the NFL, while his 83 quarterback pressures stood as the fifth-most in the NFL last season. The duo of Anderson Jr. and Hunter has produced 50.0 sacks combined since 2024, the most in the NFL.
"I was excited about paying with those guys, too," Clowney said. "Good defense, and I can help contribute and good chance to chase a Super Bowl. I know what it looks like I can help this squad."
Clowney enters the 2026 season with 66.5 career sacks, 120 tackles for loss, 16 forced fumbles and 15 fumble recoveries. His three fumble returns for scores rank as the most in the league among active players. The NFL's No. 1 total defense (277.2 total yards per game allowed in 2025) and No. 2 scoring defense (17.4 points per game allowed in 2025) is now a little richer following the addition of Clowney at the early onset of training camp.
"For sure, I was so excited. I had more opportunities. When I found out the Texans were interested, it was a no-brainer for me," Clowney said, via KPRC 2 in Houston . "It was comfortable for me to do that. I was excited to help the situation."
author: Garrett Podell

title: Bo Nix says ankle injury won't limit him in 2026: 'Nothing's holding me back'
summary: Nix and Sean Payton both said the third-year quarterback is on schedule as Denver opens training camp
full_text:
Bo is back. Third-year Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix says the fractured right ankle won't impact him in 2026.
"I feel great," Nix said . "I feel normal. Nothing's holding me back. I'm out there playing like I normally do and feel really good in my spot. I'm going to continue to push it and progress, and also continue to physically get ready for this long season. Right now, I'm exactly where I want to be for our plan, and actually was a little bit ahead of where I was last year going into the season, going into the summer. I feel really good, feel like I'm in a good spot. I think it's showing on the field."
Nix broke his ankle on the second-to-last play of overtime in the divisional round against the Buffalo Bills, leaving Broncos fans worried not only about the conference championship game but also about the 2026 season. The New England Patriots went on to defeat the Broncos 10-7 to punch their ticket to the Super Bowl .
As the fast-approaching NFL season approaches, Nix has squashed any mobility concerns.
"Absolutely not," Nix said on whether he will be limited with the ball. "I'm going to roll, and I'm going to be as athletic as I can be. It's a strength of ours and we have to use our strengths. For me, that's when I feel at my best and that's when I feel free. When I'm playing like that, when I'm moving around it's a good thing, but at the same time, I also know what it's like to not have that asset and have to stay in the pocket. I feel strong no matter what the play's going to be, no matter what happens defensively, no matter what my reaction is, I feel capable of doing it."
The Broncos will kick off their regular season with a primetime divisional game against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sept. 14. If practice continues to go as it has, fans can expect Nix to be ready to go for the Week 1 away game.
"We're right where we wanted to be, where we hoped to be at this time," coach Sean Payton said.

title: Cardinals’ Walter Nolen re-injures left calf/leg/knee? What we know.
summary: One thing the Arizona Cardinals need is the ability to stop the run. Especially up the gut. Walter Nolen was drafted in the first round out of Ole Miss last year as a major player to stop this. However, Nolen spent most of this rookie year injured. He never had an injury at any level […]
full_text: Walter Nolen III #97 (Photo by Bruce Yeung/Getty Images) | Getty Images One thing the Arizona Cardinals need is the ability to stop the run. Especially up the gut. Walter Nolen was drafted in the first round out of Ole Miss last year as a major player to stop this. Walter Nolen III is walking along the end zone with a trainer. The #AZCardinals defensive tackle appears to be limping. — Zach Gershman (@ZachAZCards) July 31, 2026 However, Nolen spent most of this rookie year injured. He never had an injury at any level until he hit the big boy club; then suddenly, he suffered a calf issue followed by a meniscus tear in December that required surgery. He did not participate in OTAs as the coaching staff was bringing him along slowly. RELATED: NOLEN LEAVES PRACTICE EARLY And now that this year’s training camp is upon us, on the first day of padded practice, Nolen was seen walking off with trainers rather gimpy. He did not return to practice. Rut ruh. What we know is that it is the same leg that he had problems with last year: his left. During a practice session with the 11-on-11 drills, he hit an offensive lineman awkwardly and then was walking with a definite limp. At first, Nolen attempted to run it off, then jog, and then walk around. But it was apparent that something was not right. Sunday, the Cardinals again take the field with an open practice from 1:45 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. Afterwards, Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur will provide a short press conference. That will be the first knowledge of exactly what is wrong with Nolen, the severity of his current status, and what the team has done as far as X-rays or an MRI. We assume it is nothing ACL-or MCL-related. The fact that he was walking and then walked the entire path off the practice field should illustrate this. More than likely, cramps are ruled out, and so far nobody has stated that his issue is anything significant. We will see at LaFleur’s presser. This 2026 defense is counting on Nolen to perform. He was limited to just six games last year, so this 2026 defense is counting on Nolen to perform. Any significant loss of game time will hurt the ability to stop the run this year. If Nolen’s injury is minor, raise your hand if the Cardinals should just shut him down for the remainder of training camp plus the preseason and then trot him out in Week 1?

title: 2026 AFC North Positional Rankings: Safety
summary: During this year’s free agency cycle and 2026 NFL draft, all four AFC North teams made significant moves to add talent to their rosters. While more additions are still possible over the next several weeks, every team’s core players are mostly set ahead of the 2026 season. How do the different positional groups in the […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - DECEMBER 07: Kyle Hamilton #14 of the Baltimore Ravens looks on before the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at M&T Bank Stadium on December 7, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images During this year’s free agency cycle and 2026 NFL draft, all four AFC North teams made significant moves to add talent to their rosters. While more additions are still possible over the next several weeks, every team’s core players are mostly set ahead of the 2026 season. How do the different positional groups in the division stack up to one another? Let’s rank the AFC North squads by position, continuing with safety. 1. Baltimore Ravens Starters : Kyle Hamilton, Malaki Starks Depth: Jaylinn Hawkins, Keondre Jackson The Ravens are anticipating a second-year jump from Malaki Starks, who had a solid rookie season in 2025 with room for improvement. Starks steadied as the season progressed and possesses star potential, which made him a worthwhile first-round pick. The Georgia product could thrive in Jesse Minter’s defensive system. Kyle Hamilton will almost surely excel in a new-look defense, as the perennial All-Pro has established himself as arguably the best safety in the NFL. Hamilton is a true chess-piece defender and will likely once again blend between playing as a deep safety, slot defender, and around the line of scrimmage. The Ravens signed veteran Jaylinn Hawks to join this group as the No. 3 safety, but he will likely see a lot of playing time. Hawkins is another sturdy versatile defensive back who can play alongside Hamilton and Starks. 2. Cincinnati Bengals Starters : Bryan Cook, Jordan Battle Depth: Kyle Dugger, PJ Jules A prized offseason acquisition for the Bengals was safety Bryan Cook from the Kansas City Chiefs. Cook posted a career-high in tackles and pass breakups last season, while grading out as PFF’s No. 4 overall safety. He ranked Top 15 in both pass coverage and run defense. Cook established himself as a full-time starter for the Chiefs three years ago and will now play the same role in Cincinnati. Alongside him is rising fourth-year player Jordan Battle, who the Bengals drafted in 2023. Battle stuffed the stat sheet last season with 125 total tackles, six pass breakups, four interceptions and two forced fumbles. The Bengals also signed veteran Kyle Dugger who joined the Steelers last season for nine games. Dugger had some productive seasons in New England but was traded away last year after being demoted to second string. If he can be a quality No. 3 safety for the Bengals, that will help stabilize their secondary even more. 3. Pittsburgh Steelers Starters: Jaquan Brisker, Deshon Elliott Depth: Darnell Savage, Sebastian Castro Returning for his third season in Pittsburgh is Deshon Elliott, who suffered a season-ending injury in 2025 and played only five games. Elliott had started 14 games for the Steelers the prior year and led the team in solo tackles with 73. Next to Elliott this coming season will be Jaquan Brisker, who the Steelers inked to a one-year contract this offseason. Brisker spent four years in Chicago as a second-round pick in 2022. He started all 52 of his played games for the Bears and played a significant role for their defense. In 2025, Brisker’s 60.4 PFF grade ranked only 67th among all safeties in over 1,000 defensive snaps. His pass rush and run defense metrics were better than his coverage grades, which tracks with his reputation as a box safety. The Steelers also signed Darnell Savage, a former first-round pick in 2019. Savage has bounced around multiple teams in recent years, so the Steelers are hoping he will find his footing in Pittsburgh. 4. Cleveland Browns Starters: Grant Delpit, Ronnie Hickman Depth: Emmanuel McNeil-Warren, Christopher Edmonds The Browns re-signed Grant Delpit to a three-year extension, ensuring he will continue being one of the team’s starting safeties. Delpit has started 68 games for the Browns since being drafted in 2021 and is coming off a career-high in forced fumbles, sacks and quarterback hits. His 66.6 overall PFF grade ranked 41st at the position. Fellow starter Ronnie Hickman was a full-time starter for the first time in 2025 and unsurprisingly also posted career-best numbers in most categories, highlighted by 103 total tackles, seven pass breakups and two interceptions. The major addition to this group is incoming rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren, who the Browns drafted with the No. 58 pick. Many believed McNeil-Warren was a first-round talent, and the Browns likely got an immediate impact player with long-term upside.

title: Buffalo Bills 2026 scouting report: TE Jackson Hawes
summary: The Buffalo Bills were fantastic when they used three tight ends last season. In fact, only the Los Angeles Rams were better on offense when using heavy personnel groupings, as the Bills came in second in EPA per play out of 13 personnel at 15.7. They were also exceptional when using two tight ends, and […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - NOVEMBER 20: Jackson Hawes #85 of the Buffalo Bills runs a route during an NFL football game against the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on November 20, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills were fantastic when they used three tight ends last season. In fact, only the Los Angeles Rams were better on offense when using heavy personnel groupings, as the Bills came in second in EPA per play out of 13 personnel at 15.7. They were also exceptional when using two tight ends , and they did so more than any other team in football. An increase in usage for Buffalo’s tight ends means that the team has to carry multiple top-flight options at the position. Or, perhaps it’s because the Bills have multiple excellent options at tight end that the team chooses to forgo spread formations, using multiple tight ends instead. Coming into the 2025 season, the top two names on the tight end depth chart received most of the attention. As the season progressed, however, it became apparent that the third man on that chart was no slouch. In today’s edition of “91 players in 91 days,” we discuss one of the best blocking tight ends in the NFL. _____________________________________________________________________________ Name: Jackson Hawes Number: 85 Position: TE Height/Weight: 6’4”, 253 pounds Age: 25 (26 on 12/6/2026) Experience/Draft: 2; selected by Buffalo in the fifth round (No. 173 overall) of the 2025 NFL Draft College: Georgia Tech Acquired: Fifth-round draft choice Financial situation (per Spotrac): Hawes enters the second year of his rookie contract, a four-year pact worth $4,520,216 overall. For the 2026 season, Hawes’ cap hit is $1,085,054 if he makes the 53-man roster. Buffalo carries a dead-cap charge of $240,162 if he’s released. 2025 Recap: Hawes likely couldn’t have dreamed of having a better rookie season. He played 43% of the Bills’ snaps on offense during the regular season, and he even made eight starts in his first year in the NFL. With Dalton Kincaid once again missing time due to myriad injury woes, it opened up some additional opportunity for Hawes, and he thrived in his role. While offensive lineman Alec Anderson served as a frequent extra blocker during the 2024 season, he isn’t a threat to catch passes like Hawes is. And while Hawes might not be the same caliber receiver as Kincaid or Dawson Knox, defenses clearly have to pay more attention to him in the passing game than they would Anderson. Hawes caught 16 passes for 187 yards and three touchdowns on 19 targets, so he made the most of his opportunities. He played in both of Buffalo’s playoff games, as well, but he wasn’t targeted in either contest. Pro Football Focus called Hawes Buffalo’s “secret superstar,” and he earned an 83.1 overall grade, which was second among all rookies and second behind only Josh Allen on Buffalo’s entire offense, as well. Positional outlook: Hawes is once again joined by Kincaid and Knox at tight end. Shane Zylstra and Keleki Latu are also on the current roster. 2026 Offseason: Hawes is healthy, having participated in all offseason work, and now training camp. 2026 Season outlook: Initially, I assumed the Bills would let Dawson Knox go, save the cap space that would come from releasing him, and move forward with Hawes as their second tight end. However, after Buffalo and Knox agreed on a renegotiated contract, that thought became a moot point. Hawes is slated to go into the 2026 season in essentially the same role he had last season, as he’ll be the run-block tight end who likely replaces Kincaid in the Bills’ 22 personnel grouping. With the improvements Knox has made as an in-line blocker throughout his career, pairing him with a legit mauler like Hawes gives Buffalo a huge advantage in the run game. They can’t tip their hand by replacing Kincaid on every running play, however, so it’s not like Hawes won’t share the field with Buffalo’s TE1 at all. There’s even a chance that Hawes does some work out of the backfield in an H-Back or fullback alignment now that Reggie Gilliam is with the New England Patriots. Head coach Joe Brady and offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael have some options, and even if Hawes stays steady and plays around 40% of the offensive snaps again, I expect that he’ll be a big part of what the team wants to do. Might Hawes do some more as a receiver? It’s possible, but ideally, the Bills just have a healthy Kincaid available to see more targets, which would allow Hawes to continue doing what he does best — mauling would-be tacklers at the point of attack. There’s room for growth as a receiver, and Hawes already showed that he has reliable hands in a small sample size last year. Unless you play in a fantasy football league that rewards blockers, Jackson Hawes likely isn’t someone you should pick. However, if you were starting a real football team, Hawes is exactly the kind of tight end you want on your side. He’s a lock for the roster and his role is clear moving forward.
