title: Cowboys camp report: 3 things we learned, 3 things we still need to see after 3 practices
summary: Dallas opened its 20th training camp in Oxnard with three practices before taking Sunday off ahead of Monday’s first padded session. Here’s what stood out across practices one (Wednesday, July 29), two (Thursday, July 30), and three (Saturday, August 1). Three Things We Learned Caleb Downs is going to be everywhere. The 11th overall pick […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - JULY 30: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer of the Dallas Cowboys speaks with members of the media during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on July 30, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images Dallas opened its 20th training camp in Oxnard with three practices before taking Sunday off ahead of Monday’s first padded session. Here’s what stood out across practices one (Wednesday, July 29), two (Thursday, July 30), and three (Saturday, August 1). Three Things We Learned Caleb Downs is going to be everywhere. The 11th overall pick didn’t ease into his first NFL camp – he lined up at nickel, in the box, off the edge, and deep in the secondary, sometimes shifting spots within a single play, and came away with a fumble recovery off a Rashan Gary strip on his very first day. DeMarvion Overshown explains his (and the team’s) early impressions of Downs: "We're not even looking at [Caleb Downs] as a rookie. We're looking at him as a guy that's going to change this defense around, going to change the culture. He's won at every level of football." DeMarvion Overshown believes Caleb Downs is an immediate difference maker for the… pic.twitter.com/j32PMLixOd — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) July 31, 2026 Jaishawn Barham is pushing for real defensive snaps far sooner than expected. The third-round rookie has looked comfortable as an off-ball linebacker through the first three practices, flashing well enough to get a Brian Schottenheimer shout out for his ability to get off blocks and be in on tackles, and got a lot of work with the starters in the second and third practices. The Twitterverse is all aflutter: DLLS Cowboys: Jaishawn Barham is gonna be the starting middle linebacker . Marcus Mosher: The next Baun ? Kiser: BARHAMMER!!! The offense is spreading the ball around more than expected. It’s not just Lamb and Pickens – Javonte Williams, Jonathan Mingo, and others have all had moments through the first practices, a sign the offense isn’t just a two-man show. In the second practice, Prescott targeted seven different receivers on 13 observed throws . Just as importantly, the red-zone offense already looks sharper with Prescott’s red-zone touchdowns on Saturday going to four different targets. Improving red-zone efficiency was a stated point of emphasis entering camp, and Saturday’s session backed it up. Per Todd Archer : “Dak Prescott had touchdown passes to CeeDee Lamb on the post, two to Ryan Flournoy (dig, slot fade) and a bullet of a throw low to the outside that receiver George Pickens corralled for the score. There was one interception when a Prescott checkdown was tipped by running back Jaydon Blue into the arms of safety Malik Hooker.“ Three Things We Still Need To See Can Jaydon Blue prove he can be the RB2 rather than simply look like the most explosive back? That distinction matters because the padded practices will reveal things that shorts don’t: pass protection, contact balance, physicality, ball security, etc. Blue has looked good in shorts , but real contact starting Monday is the next real test of the RB2 race behind Javonte Williams. Can Jonathan Mingo pull away from Marquez Valdes-Scantling and the rest of the receiver room? Behind the Lamb-Pickens-Flournoy trio, the fifth (and maybe sixth) receiver spot is still up for grabs, and the next several practices should start sorting out who’s separating from the pack . And don’t underestimate the rookie receivers. UDFA rookie wide receiver Camden Brown had the “catch of the day” during Saturday’s practice, hauling in a back-pylon fade from Sam Howell for a TD. He’s an intriguing size/athleticism bet at the bottom of a crowded receiver room. Seventh-round rookie Anthony Smith is also making plays. How the retooled defense responds to Monday’s first padded practice. Three straight practices in helmets-and-shorts have shown promise, but BTB’s own early-camp notes flagged that “ when the pads come on, things will really heat up .” That’s the next real proving ground. Across three practices, per Calvin Watkins , Prescott is lighting it up, going 12-15 on Saturday, 14-17 on Thursday, and 11-15 on Wednesday. While unofficial, that’s 37-47 over three days, a completion rate of 79%. It’s encouraging, but it’s also exactly the kind of number that needs a giant training-camp asterisk. The pads aren’t on, the throws are largely scripted, and nobody is keeping an official stat sheet for a reason. Over the same span, Joe Milton went 14-22 (64%) and Sam Howell 12-21 (57%), which probably says more about the quality of the backup QBs than the quality of the defense. Still, Prescott’s efficiency, combined with the distribution of the ball and the early red-zone results, is one of the more encouraging offensive signals through three practices – and a challenge for the defense. Three Things That Haven’t Changed Lamb and Prescott are still automatic together. The middle of the field remained friendly territory for the two of them through three practices, continuing one of the most reliable connections in football rather than revealing anything new. George Pickens is locked in. With his franchise-tag situation settled, Pickens arrived engaged, not distracted – exactly the version of him the Cowboys were hoping to see after a clean offseason, and not the largely media-driven narrative of “drama.” We really made it to training camp with no drama. https://t.co/8NCEp1nDQ7 — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) July 27, 2026 Dallas came into camp about as healthy as a team can be. DaRon Bland and Donovan Ezeiruaku, both coming off offseason surgery, remain on a “monitored” workload plan rather than any injury list. Through three practices, safeties Jalen Thompson (hip), P.J. Locke (knee), and Zion Childress (hamstring) are the only players missing time, though none of their injuries have appeared serious enough so far to disrupt the bigger picture. In their place, others step up. Safeties Alijah Clark and Markquese Bell shared the work with the first-team defense, but one down-roster guy stood out. Best defender in practice #3 for @dallascowboys might have been safety Rudy Wood, getting snaps with Thompson & Locke out. Vets & coaches noticed him. A few players here battling for backup spots who might have battled to be starters last year. — Brad Sham (@Boys_Vox) August 1, 2026 What Else Stood Out Communication: DeMarvion Overshown is wearing the defensive green dot, running Christian Parker’s play calls from the middle linebacker spot. Coaches have already tested him with simulated communication breakdowns between Parker and the headset. Schottenheimer said Overshown got the defense lined up correctly regardless. Schottenheimer said in addition to DeMarvion Overshown, rookie Caleb Downs, Shemar James, and Curtis Robinson (likely a backup green dot/CJ Goodwin replacement on special teams) are also wearing the green dot. Caleb Downs getting the green dot just reiterates the Overshown quote from above: “ We’re not even looking at [Caleb Downs] as a rookie. We’re looking at him as a guy that’s going to change this defense around .” Leadership: Schottenheimer named an 11-player leadership council to open camp: QB Dak Prescott, WR CeeDee Lamb, RB Javonte Williams, TE Jake Ferguson, OL Tyler Smith, OL Tyler Booker, DT Quinnen Williams, DT Kenny Clark, OLB Rashan Gary, S Jalen Thompson and P Bryan Anger. It’s a mix of established voices (Prescott, Lamb, Smith, Ferguson) and newcomers Schottenheimer wants to fast-track into the locker room (Clark, Gary, Thompson, Quinnen Williams — all first- or second-year Cowboys). But it’s more than just old-versus-new: Schottenheimer appears to be deliberately building a leadership structure around the team’s new physical identity. The roster has been reshaped around the lines, and now the leadership council is disproportionately populated by them. That emphasis on the lines is exactly what former safety Darren Woodson, three-time Super…

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 42
summary: It is Day 42 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: (Original Caption) Dallas Cowboys Bob Hayes (22) takes a punt during the first quarter and runs it back 64 yards to the Cleveland Browns 13-yard line. Dallas went on to score a few plays later. Dallas was leading the Browns 24-7 at halftime. That's John DeMarie (55) who missed Hayes. It is Day 42 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Welcome to Day 42 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit the game that gave the Cowboys their first postseason victory and established them as a legitimate championship-level franchise. Dallas and Cleveland had both finished 9-5, but there was nothing even about what happened on Christmas Eve in 1967. Sunday, December 24, 1967 — 2:30 p.m. ET Cotton Bowl, Dallas, Texas Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 52, Cleveland Browns 14 Dallas took control of this one immediately. The Cowboys drove 80 yards in 13 plays on their opening possession, with Don Perkins breaking a 24-yard run before Don Meredith found Craig Baynham for a three-yard touchdown. Later in the first quarter, Bob Hayes returned a punt 64 yards to the Cleveland 13-yard line. Four plays later, Perkins powered across on fourth down, and Dallas had a 14-0 lead before the Browns could settle into the game. Cleveland briefly threatened to respond when star running back Leroy Kelly broke a 46-yard run to the Dallas 10. The Cowboys defense stiffened, however, and a poor snap ruined Lou Groza’s field-goal attempt. Dallas took over at its own 10-yard line, and two plays later Meredith launched the play that broke the game open. Hayes raced past cornerback Mike Howell, caught the ball beyond midfield and completed an 86-yard touchdown, giving the Cowboys a 21-0 advantage. It was the longest scoring play in NFL postseason history at the time. Danny Villanueva added a short field goal to make it 24-0 before Cleveland finally reached the end zone. Frank Ryan found tight end Milt Morin for a 13-yard touchdown late in the second quarter, cutting the score to 24-7 at halftime. The Browns had at least given themselves a small opening, but Dallas removed it almost immediately after the break. The third quarter became an avalanche, and if you were a Cowboys fan this quarter was a dream come true. Baynham scored on a one-yard run, Perkins added another short touchdown and defensive back Cornell Green intercepted Ryan and returned it 60 yards for a score. Dallas piled up 21 unanswered points in the quarter and carried a 45-7 lead into the fourth. What had begun as an important conference playoff game had become one of the most one-sided postseason performances of the era. Baynham scored his third touchdown of the afternoon on another one-yard run, pushing Dallas past 50 points. Cleveland’s Paul Warfield later caught a 75-yard touchdown from Ryan, but it did nothing beyond changing the final margin. The Cowboys had scored in every quarter, produced six offensive touchdowns and added Green’s interception return in a 52-14 rout. This game belongs on the countdown because it marked a major step in the Cowboys’ transformation from an expansion team into one of the NFL’s emerging powers. Dallas had reached the NFL Championship Game the previous season but lost to Green Bay without first having to win a playoff round. Beating Cleveland gave the organization its first postseason victory, the Eastern Conference title and another opportunity against Vince Lombardi’s Packers. Seven days later, the Cowboys would play in the Ice Bowl, one of the most famous games in NFL history. #Cowboys vs #Browns 1967 Divisional Round Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 52, Cleveland Browns 14 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/WlWJmyvgfI — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 1, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game This remains tied for the highest-scoring postseason game in Cowboys history. The 52 points was tied in the Super Bowl versus Buffalo, but the 38-point winning margin is still a franchise playoff record. summary: The Dallas Cowboys have packed away three practices at training camp so far, and while there are a lot of new things to watch, some of what we expected going in is playing out. full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - JULY 30: Caleb Downs #13 of the Dallas Cowboys defends during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on July 30, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys have packed away three practices at training camp so far, and while there are a lot of new things to watch, some of what we expected going in is playing out. Here are three things we expected that are happening. Caleb Downs is a chess piece As many people predicted, Caleb Downs is being used all over the field. He’s dropping into the box, he’s played nickel back, and with Jalen Thompson and P.J. Locke out Saturday, he started at deep safety in the base 3-4, before rotating back into the nickel back position. Downs’ versatility has stood out thus far; he’s even mixed it up a bit with Brevyn Spann-Ford after Spann-Ford dropped a would-be completion. Downs nearly had an interception after fellow rookie Malachi Lawrence rushed Dak Prescott and drew a hurried throw. It will be intriguing to see what else they ask of Downs, but so far, we’ve see a ton of versatility from the rookie. Brevyn Spann-Ford didn’t like Caleb Downs knocking the ball out of his hands after this incompletion. BSF gave the rook a shove after the play. pic.twitter.com/7VzOQSTAYr — Mike Leslie (@MikeLeslieWFAA) August 1, 2026 George Pickens is shining What can be said about the receiver that hasn’t already been said? Pickens has looked fantastic to start camp; we all knew he would be a handful for this defense, but Saturday’s red-zone drill further demonstrated his ability as a pass-catcher. Pickens had Shavon Revel draped all over him and used a perfectly placed ball from Prescott, his inside leverage and his body to seal the TD catch from Revel. Granted, that was a coachable moment for Revel on positional defense, but Pickens still made it all look so easy. As training camp ramps up, Pickens’ play will continue to show through and hopefully help sharpen and test these defenders. 4-2-3 pic.twitter.com/yiUF7IJBrQ — Nick Eatman (@nickeatman) August 1, 2026 The offense looks as good as advertised Pickens hasn’t been the only one who has played well so far; the Cowboys’ offense has been humming. Prescott has been accurate, the receivers have made contested catches, and the running game has looked explosive, to some people’s surprise, mostly because of Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah. Some contested drops aside, everybody on the offensive side of the ball looks confident and locked in. With the continuity that the Cowboys maintained on the side of the ball, that shouldn’t come as a surprise to anybody.

title: 3 biggest surprises so far at training camp
summary: Three practices are in the books for the Dallas Cowboys out in Oxnard at training camp. They haven’t put the pads on yet, but things did pick up a bit on Saturday as far as the intensity and plays being made. Guys are flying around and settling into camp nicely, and that will only ramp […]
full_text: Three practices are in the books for the Dallas Cowboys out in Oxnard at training camp. They haven’t put the pads on yet, but things did pick up a bit on Saturday as far as the intensity and plays being made. Guys are flying around and settling into camp nicely, and that will only ramp up in the next few weeks. Quarterback Dak Prescott is looking sharp, and his connections with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are cooking. Rookie safety Caleb Downs has been all over the field, and Cobie Durant looks fantastic. Those things were expected to happen once the Cowboys hit camp, but there are some other things that have happened that weren’t on the menu. Here are three surprises so far out in Oxnard. Cowboys linked to trade for All-Pro LB Jordyn Brooks The Cowboys selected Jaishawn Barham in the third round, and he’s been flashing so far at camp. Plus, they added Dee Winters during the offseason. They will battle it out at middle linebacker, but Dallas could be interested in another. According to Bryan Broaddus, the Cowboys might be looking at trading for All-Pro middle linebacker Jordyn Brooks of the Miami Dolphins. Bryan Broaddus tells @gavindawson & @EricChiofalo to "keep an eye on (Dolphins LB) Jordyn Brooks" as a Cowboys' trade target: "I think they're going for a bigger fish (than Bobby Wagner). … The team I think you need to focus on is Miami…." pic.twitter.com/JUCs6qSRru — 105.3 The FAN (@1053thefan) July 31, 2026 This is shocking because Miami signed Brooks to a three-year extension worth $51.3 million with $35 million guaranteed recently. However, the idea isn’t as wild as some would think. His base salary over the first three years of his deal up to a little over $27 million which isn’t a lot at all. The cap hit for Brooks in 2026 if he was traded would be $6.16 million, which is minimal as well. Plus, the Dolphins would only take on $4.95 million in dead money if they dealt him. This makes the trade extremely doable. It’s probably a longshot, and a guy like veteran Bobby Wagner is more realistic. With that said, it’s something to monitor. Tyler Guyton gets snaps at right tackle It’s no secret that Guyton is entering the most important season of his short career. He’s trying to prove that he’s the guy at left tackle, and that he was worth a first-round pick in 2024. An interesting development did come about in regards to Guyton at practice on Saturday. He took snaps with the second team at right tackle. Tyler Guyton getting some second-team work at right tackle pic.twitter.com/pRfnibVMwu — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) August 1, 2026 In college at Oklahoma, Guyton logged over 1,000 snaps at right tackle, so he’s very family with playing the position. Guyton himself has said that being on the left feels more natural to him, which brings up the question of what is the reason for this experiment? The Cowboys did draft left tackle Drew Shelton in the fourth round, and Nate Thomas is also included in the competition at that spot. Terence Steele has been serviceable at right tackle over the last few years. Perhaps the Cowboys just want to see if Guyton could possibly play that spot even better, That would create a scenario where they could shuffle the line but would need a solution at left tackle. Is that Tyler Smith? We shall see. Phil Mafah looks more explosive When the Cowboys drafted Phil Mafah in the seventh round in 2025, he came in with a similar running style to starter Javonte Williams. That tough, downhill type of runner that can physically punish opposing defenses. In the first several days of camp, something has looked a little different, his explosiveness. When Mafah has had the ball in his hands at camp, he’s had an extra gear. He looks faster and more shifty in his movements. At 6-foot-1 and 235 pounds, Mafah could seriously challenge for quite a bit of playing time if he can consistently show this burst and stack good days as he battles Jaydon Blue for RB2 duties. His offseason work that has focused on being more explosive has paid off big so far. Dallas Cowboys RB Phil Mafah getting more EXPLOSIVE‼️ .. here's how 👀 #cowboys #nfl #cowboysnation #dallas #fyp pic.twitter.com/PsxDUGP9bC — J Tuck (@jtuck151) August 1, 2026

title: Surprise Cowboys draft pick is popping at camp
summary: If we were to evaluate the Dallas Cowboys defense so far in training camp, you’d get the impression that the team is looking pretty good. That’s not too surprising. With Christian Parker installing his new defense and the Cowboys having some talent around the unit, hopes are high. But one problem position that many still […]
full_text: May 1, 2026; Frisco, TX, USA; Dallas Cowboys linebacker Jaishawn Barham (55) catches a pass during practice at the Ford Center at the Star Training Facility in Frisco, Texas. Mandatory Credit: Chris Jones-Imagn Images | Chris Jones-Imagn Images If we were to evaluate the Dallas Cowboys defense so far in training camp, you’d get the impression that the team is looking pretty good. That’s not too surprising. With Christian Parker installing his new defense and the Cowboys having some talent around the unit, hopes are high. But one problem position that many still talk about is the linebacker corps. What has been eyebrow-raising is how much the front office has discussed player acquisition through external outlets, especially coming from Stephen Jones. When he mentions the Cowboys aren’t done adding outside help, you tend to lean forward in your seat. Now, where exactly do the Cowboys need more support? This week, we’ve heard rumors about Maxx Crosby once more but also about Miami Dolphins’ linebacker Jordyn Brooks. Bryan Broaddus sparked some discussion about Dallas adding the veteran defender. “I think they’re looking bigger than Bobby Wagner. That’s what I would tell you guys,” Broaddus said while speaking on 105.3 The Fan. Broaddus had a target in mind as well, saying that the Cowboys could be going after a “bigger fish.” He used the word fish intentionally, saying he believes the Miami Dolphins are still willing to trade linebacker Jordyn Brooks, and that Dallas would be interested in bringing him in. “I think they’re going for a bigger fish. Big fish. Yeah, and please take the word fish in mind here when I say this. But, yeah, I think they’ve got a linebacker in mind,” Broaddus said. First of all, Miami has made it clear that Brooks isn’t going anywhere and is a big part of their plans this season. Secondly, do the Cowboys need more at interior linebacker? From what we’ve seen thus far from a promising insider linebacker, the Cowboys might be good in that department, and it may be better to get this player on the field sooner rather than later. Jaishawn Barham, the other Cowboys rookie we should be talking about We get it. Cowboys Nation should be thrilled to have Caleb Downs, as he was arguably the best defender in the draft. In fact, Downs is so special a prospect that he overshadows the entire rookie draft class that includes fellow first-round pick Malachi Lawrence. Yet, Jaishawn Barham has commanded our attention over the first few days at training camp. He has fans excited about his versatility. Barham has caught the attention of the coaching staff, with head coach Brian Schottenheimer already singing his praises within the first week of camp. What we already know about Barham is he has ideal size and strength to play inside linebacker for the Cowboys. Yet, what we’re seeing is he has the smarts and awareness. On this one play, he did an excellent job finding his way to the backfield on what would’ve been a tackle for loss. Jaishawn Barham probably would’ve blown this play up. pic.twitter.com/HHUDGEsk2J — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) August 1, 2026 He then followed that up later, with great instincts on this play here for a pass breakup. Jaishawn Barham goal line PBU. He’s been getting a lot of work with the starters today. pic.twitter.com/k7woV4yEHp — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) August 1, 2026 Whether it’s stopping the run or defending the pass, Barham has earned an opportunity to see the field more. Clearly the coaching staff agrees, as he took on work with the starting defense. While you can never have enough help on a roster with high ambitions, Barham has only piqued curiosity of what more he can do and how much more he can grow before the season opener. Could one of the biggest enigmatic positions on the roster possibly become a strength? Think about it: Jaisahwn Barham, DeMarvion Overshown, and Dee Winters could be a strong trio if everything goes right – Overshown stays healthy, Winters repeats his breakout from last year, and Barham continues on his current trajectory. Dallas might have created a very competitive inside linebacker group where everyone is on near equal footing, with the linebacker with the least experience flashing almost daily. With days like Barham has had early in camp, it could make the Joneses decide to acquire talent at another postion.

title: Cowboys defense is starting to take shape
summary: After one week of practices in Oxnard, California, the Dallas Cowboys are quickly turning grief into relief when it comes to their defense. Following a complete overhaul of both the coaching staff and roster, this revamped unit boasts a completely different identity, and there are already several standouts demanding our attention. While it is still […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Oxnard, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker at training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After one week of practices in Oxnard, California, the Dallas Cowboys are quickly turning grief into relief when it comes to their defense. Following a complete overhaul of both the coaching staff and roster, this revamped unit boasts a completely different identity, and there are already several standouts demanding our attention. While it is still early in training camp, the collective excitement surrounding the new regime is already translating into tangible, high-energy results on the practice field. Here is what we learned about the Cowboys’ defense during week one. Trenches Rashan Gary has brought a fierce veteran presence to the defensive line, showing why he’s such a good fit for Parker’s defense. As a dirt-pinning 4-3 guy, he’s been giving Terence Steele fits attacking with a full-speed rush, disrupting the tempo. He’s also shown his stand-up 3-4 versatility running down receivers along the outside. He’s always attacking and already forced a fumble during the first practice of training camp . Another edge earning high praise early is Donovan Ezeiruaku. Most importantly, he’s been fully cleared after rehabbing from hip surgery. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer has indicated that he looks like the Ezeiruaku of old after reviewing the film of day one, revealing that he had three would-be sacks during the team’s first practice. Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark have looked good together and are proving to be a formidable force along the interior defensive line. Their strength and athleticism have made it difficult for the offensive line to gain any traction in the running game. Middle The linebacker group is very interesting as the coaching staff is throwing all kinds of tests at them. They challenged their leader by cutting the communications in DeMarvion Overshown’s helmet to see how he could handle a high-stress situation, and he passed with flying colors. Parker has been rotating first-team reps between Dee Winters and Jaishawn Barham, using staggered looks alongside Overshown. Winters will move back in coverage while Barham is more of a creeper at the line of scrimmage. Barham has been coming on stronger with each new day. Sometimes he steps up and attacks the backfield , while at other times, he’ll slide back into coverage. He had a nice pass breakup on Saturday , preventing a completion to CeeDee Lamb over the middle. This versatility allows Parker to keep their intentions secret until the last minute. Parker is also trying to get a better feel for what he can do with linebacker Marist Luifau. There’s been a lot of talk about moving him around, and based on the first week of practice, they’re walking the walk. Literally. Luifau is walking around, moving to different spots, sometimes on the same play. He’ll start inside, then walk down to the outside like he’s going to attack the quarterback, only to bounce back to middle linebacker before the ball is snapped. It’s unclear where this will ultimately lead, but Parker is trying out stuff. Secondary The cornerback hierarchy put Shavon Revel Jr. as the odd man out in the first couple of practices, but he found more action on Saturday. DaRon Bland and free agent Cobie Durant have been primarily handling the boundary spots, but this isn’t a knock on Revel Jr., as the veterans have looked really good. The best bit of news is that Bland is moving well, showing no lingering effects of his foot injury. On one rep specifically, he read the play well, planted his foot in the dirt, closed quickly, and cleanly got around Breyvan Spann-Ford for a nice pass breakup . That’s a sight for sore eyes. And the news of Durant shouldn’t be tossed aside. He is smothering receivers, not biting on fakes, showing how he could be one of the team’s sneakiest best acquisitions this offseason. Revel Jr. had a rough time dealing with George Pickens, but to be fair, everyone is having a rough time with Pickens. While the team’s talented wideout has been hauling in contested catches, at least we can say they’re being contested. Revel Jr. has been draped all over him, so that’s promising, but the veteran receiver is putting the young corner through the wringer. Oh, Caleb Downs. How do we love thee? Let us count the ways. It’s fun to watch a guy who has elevated expectations live up to the hype. The rookie safety is right in the thick of things, hanging with wideouts, dropping down in the box, or strolling back to cover deep middle. He’s everywhere. His fluid movement is fun to watch, but so is his focused energy. He’s always so ready to make the play and was there to pounce on the Gary punch-out for a nice fumble recovery. He did get humbled on one play when he learned that CeeDee Lamb might be a little better in the slot than he is right now, but overall, the rookie is moving well, dialed in, and off to a promising start. While the rookie gets all the attention, the veteran Jalen Thompson is doing some impressing of his own. Right from the get-go he was diagnosing looks from the offense, shouting out last-second adjustments, and then flying sideline-to-sideline when the ball is snapped. Thompson sat out of practice on Saturday as he was nursing a hip injury, as did P.J. Locke, who is dealing with a knee injury from earlier in the week. This opened the door for Markquese Bell to see a little more action. Overall, the defense has looked good with the challenges they’ve faced. The defensive line has packed some punch and shown some explosiveness, the linebackers are demonstrating some much-needed versatility, and the safeties continue to impress, providing a lot of optimism for this group. The excitement in Southern California is undeniable as this multiple, hard-hitting defense continues to build something meaningful. So far, so good for Parker’s troops.
author: Dan Rogers

title: Cowboys news: Dallas o-line elite in one area, suspect in another
summary: Cowboys offensive line praise comes with one unavoidable condition – Marcus Mosher, The Landry Hat The praise that comes at a price. No team in the NFL has invested more into their offensive line than the Dallas Cowboys over the last five years. The Cowboys have spent three first-round picks on the unit since the […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - DECEMBER 14: Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) backs into the pocket behind his offensive line during the game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Minnesota Vikings on December 14, 2025 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Matthew Pearce/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Cowboys offensive line praise comes with one unavoidable condition – Marcus Mosher, The Landry Hat The praise that comes at a price. No team in the NFL has invested more into their offensive line than the Dallas Cowboys over the last five years. The Cowboys have spent three first-round picks on the unit since the 2022 draft and have used another third-round choice (Cooper Beebe) on their starting center. There are several teams across the league who have not taken a single first-round offensive lineman in the last decade, let alone three in five years. But the Cowboys believe their offensive line, specifically their interior offensive line , can be the strength of their team. The truth is, it better be, considering all of the resources and assets they’ve used to address the group. Despite all of the resources spent, this has not been an elite unit over the last few years. However, Dallas is hopeful that it will change in 2026. In a recent article by offensive line expert Brandon Thorn, he ranked all 32 offensive lines heading into the NFL over on Establish The Run . The Cowboys did make an appearance inside the top 10, coming in at No. 9. Thorn also joined the Locked On Cowboys Podcast recently and mentioned that he would have ranked this unit higher if the rankings weren’t slanted toward pass protection over run blocking (Establish The Run is a fantasy football website, and his OL rankings are weighted more towards passing). Tyler Guyton will determine the ceiling of the Cowboys’ talented offensive line One of the reasons why Thorn was so optimistic about the Cowboys’ offensive line this year was due to the interior offensive linemen on the roster, including Tyler Smith and Tyler Booker. This has a chance to be the best guard duo in all of the league, and if Cooper Beebe can continue to develop (Thorn is high on Beebe), there is no reason they can’t dominate upfront. Comparing the 2 Dallas Cowboys linebacker options – Mark Heaney, Inside the Star The Cowboys could fortify their young linebacker group with either one of these veteran choices. Training camp may be underway, but the main story following America’s Team this past week was the front office alluding to additional roster moves being made. Owner and General Manager Jerry Jones made it clear that Dallas is still in the trade market, and an addition to the Cowboys linebacker room makes the most sense. Sure, Maxx Crosby could also make sense, but I think Dallas is comfortable with their EDGE room, at least for now. In my eyes, that leaves the linebacker position as the most likely place they are thinking of adding to. It was their worst group last season, and while Dee Winters and Jaishawn Barham are nice additions, they could use a true top dog in the room. Two options in particular stand out, and that’s what we’ll get into here; this is a quick overview and comparison between free agent Bobby Wagner and Dolphins star Jordyn Brooks. Bobby Wagner Overview: Long-Time NFL Veteran Still Produces (36 Y/O, 162 Total Tackles for Washington in 2025, All-Pro in 2024). “B-Wags” has been filling up the tackle sheet in the NFL since 2012, and this is the first time he has really been left without a team. The 36-year-old former Seahawk, Ram, and Commander, has been rumored to be a Cowboys target for a long time, but this seems like the first real chance at it becoming a reality. Wagner’s 11-year All-Pro streak (insane stat right there) was broken last season, as his numbers took a slight downturn and his actual performance did seem like that of a nearly 40-year-old linebacker. The speed and quickness just isn’t as elite as it once was. Still, he’s a fantastic IQ and locker room player, productive, and would clearly be a starter for Dallas. He isn’t a long-term fix like Brooks, but he is a logical low-cost band-aid on a big issue for Dallas. Tough news about the Cowboys’ most double-teamed defensive linemen – Reid Hanson, Cowboys Wire The numbers don’t lie. Despite posting a league-leading 31.2 pressure rate, the Dallas Cowboys only ranked 22nd in actual sack production. With Micah Parsons no longer demanding double-teams in Dallas, offenses feasted against the Cowboys’ struggling pass rush. For years, Parsons demanded all the attention, absorbing double-teams and making life easier on his teammates in the process. Without Parsons, everyone had to do their part. The thing about double-teams is that they’re unavoidable. Most plays, the numbers are engineered to work in an offense’s favor, so someone has to face it. In 2025 it was a surprising collection of defenders who had the highest double-team rate for the Cowboys and unfortunately two of those players are no longer in Dallas here in 2026. As hard as it is to believe, the Cowboy who demanded the highest double-team rate was Solomon Thomas. Based on PFF play tracking, Thomas’ 67.40 double-team percentage was 12 th in the NFL. For a guy that only played 227 pass rush snaps that’s pretty good. Thomas moved on to the Tennessee Titans over the offseason and no longer factors into the Cowboys’ equation this year. The second most double-teamed lineman in Dallas was Kenny Clark. His production might have dipped in 2025 but respect from offenses remain intact. Clark is back in 2026, but his role in Christian Parker’s system is a source of concern. Clark may have to man the nose tackle spot in the 3-4 if other options don’t work out. It will guarantee a heavy dose of doubles but will take a chunk out of his pressures in the process. In his time split between the New York Jets and the Cowboys, Quinnen Williams was double-teamed at a rate of 65.6 percent. It’s not far off from the league leaders and he saw a good deal of success through it all. Great things are expected of him in 2026, so he represents the hope for the new season. The fourth Cowboy defender on the list is Osa Odighizuwa. Like Thomas, he’s no longer with the team and will need to be replaced internally. It just so happens Odighizuwa was chipped at a higher rate than the previous three, but he typically posted good numbers as an interior pass rusher despite it all. Interior players dominated the list. It shouldn’t be surprising since the nature of their technique almost guarantees high double-team numbers. Good interior players who demand attention means edge players get to operate in space more often. It seems to be the blueprint of the Cowboys’ roster but requires dominant and feared interior players to make it work. Jerry Jones offered surprising update on curtains at Cowboys games – R.J. Ochoa, Blogging the Boys Let there (not) be light. Finally. We all know the drill by now. Around the third quarter of the afternoon games at AT&T Stadium… it happens. The time of year means that the sun shines through the glass of the building and provides lighting that makes for incredible photographs and pieces of art. Cool. None of that matters relative to the objective that the building is supposed to serve, though. At least the primary objective. Many a Cowboys player have complained about the sun and its glare through the building, and at every turn Jerry Jones has said that he isn’t doing anything about it. Jerry spoke to Mike Doocy on Saturday and said that the Cowboys were giving a thought to tinting the windows the way that FIFA did for the World Cup matches that the building hosted this summer (you know, the ones at “Dallas Stadium”). It is worth noting that the afternoon sun and the impact it has on the building is different in June than October, but the point is/was that FIFA did not take a chance that the play on the field would be compromised. Obviously Jerry…

title: 2026 Denver Broncos Training Camp: 5 things we have learned
summary: Denver Broncos training camp is off and rolling, and the team has been on the practice field for two ramp-up practices and two official camp practices with fans in attendance. It’s still very early into the process, and the pads have not come on yet; that’s on Monday, but we have learned a few things […]
full_text: ENGLEWOOD, CO - JULY 31: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos throws a pass during training camp at Broncos Park Powered by CommonSpirit on July 31, 2026 in Englewood, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Getty Images) | Getty Images Denver Broncos training camp is off and rolling, and the team has been on the practice field for two ramp-up practices and two official camp practices with fans in attendance. It’s still very early into the process, and the pads have not come on yet; that’s on Monday, but we have learned a few things about this team this week. So, with all that said, here are the five things we have learned about the Denver Broncos through the first four practices for training camp. Jonathon Cooper is practicing Heading into training camp, the status of Broncos starting edge rusher Jonathon Cooper seemed very much up in the air. He was arrested twice during the offseason and is going through the legal process right now. That led many fans and media, myself included, to speculate about his future with the team. The last time we heard from Payton, he expressed his disappointment with the matter, and it seemed to put Cooper’s status with the team in hot water. However, to Cooper’s credit, he attended a 40-day inpatient mental health and wellness counseling program and seemed to be working on himself after his off-the-field incident. The team must have been happy with the results because Cooper reported to camp with the rest of his teammates and has been participating throughout the week without limitations. Sean Payton gives an update on Jonathon Cooper: Says Cooper’s been “fantastic” working away from the building and they are monitoring the situation closely pic.twitter.com/IeJuFh8uWs — DNVR Broncos (@DNVR_Broncos) July 29, 2026 Head Coach Sean Payton was asked about Cooper, and he told reporters that they are staying the course with the league and club protocol but added that Cooper has been “fantastic working away from the building”. “We’re staying the course with the league. We’re staying the course with league protocol, club protocol relative to what we’re advised to do. He’s been fantastic working away from the building, and we’ll continue to do that and monitor it. We’re supportive, and yet very much aware of the seriousness of these types of things. Pretty much what I said in the spring, there’s a schedule and a course to this, and that’s what we have to follow.” Payton was later asked if they’re waiting for Cooper’s legal process to play out before making a decision on his future with the team. He repeated that they’re going through the league process but again added that they are proud of the work Cooper has done and that he is fully supportive of him right now and that they are still gathering all the information. “There’s a process relative to the league, relative to the legal process and then as that all comes together, we can make the right decision. And that’s simply it. There’s no follow up, there’s no other underlying… It’s today’s protocol, and there are probably maybe a dozen players in other camps that are kind of going through a similar protocol. We’re proud of the work he did these last, call it month and a half. It wasn’t easy, and it’ll continue to be a challenge. We’ll see where it goes. [I am] fully supportive of him right now as we gather all the information and then we go from there.” Payton did hint that Cooper’s legal situation could be finalized “sooner rather than later. “ so we may have some sort of settlement before Cooper’s late August arraignment date, but that’s just speculation on my part. The fact that Cooper is with the team and practicing and Payton is speaking positively about him is a clear sign that he will likely remain with the team. The legal process is still ongoing and discipline from the league could still happen, but at the very least, Cooper’s future with the team looks a lot better right now than it did a week ago. Nix and the offense look good early I have covered many Broncos training camps at this point in my life, and one thing has remained consistent throughout many of them. The offense struggles early on. Part of that reason is that the Broncos’ offenses were not very good, the quarterbacks sucked, and/or the coaching wasn’t very good. Some combination of those three things. We even saw them start slow last season before turning it on later in camp. However, this year, quarterback Bo Nix and the Broncos offense have come out of the gates on fire. "Nothing's holding me back." QB Bo Nix feels 'really good' in early days of #BroncosCamp » https://t.co/2JsyVeMNV7 pic.twitter.com/A4kiZNCDWQ — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) August 2, 2026 Nix has hit multiple deep passes throughout camp, including a 50-yard bomb to Marvin Mims and another 40+ yarder to Pat Bryant. Nix also doesn’t look impacted by his offseason ankle surgery that cost him the vast majority of his offseason. Oh yeah, his chemistry with Jaylen Waddle looks great, and the two have been connecting throughout camp. It’s early, very early, but it’s a great sign that this Broncos offense is looking this good early in camp against a good defense. It hasn’t been without flaws, of course; the defense has had its share of wins, but the fact we’re talking about the offense looking good early in camp is an exciting development. New offensive coordinator and playcaller Davis Webb is looking to make an impact on this offense, and so far, the results have been great. Based on reports, we have seen more uptempo, quicker to the line, some creativity, and more use of motion. It remains to be seen how much of that will carry over into the regular season, but I am intrigued to see how it all plays out. Mims for WR3? One of the more interesting camp battles happening is for the Broncos’ WR3 job. Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton are expected to be the Broncos’ top pass-catching options this upcoming season, but the snaps and targets behind those two are up for grabs. The three main contenders are Troy Franklin, Marvin Mims, and Pat Bryant. All three players flashed at different times last season and can make a strong case for the job. However, early in camp, one player has stood out amongst the rest thus far, and that player has been Marvin Mims Jr. He simply has been making plays throughout camp. He has caught long touchdown passes from Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham and has been heavily targeted during the Broncos 11 on 11 team periods. Marvin Mims keeps getting open and keeps making plays. — Aric DiLalla (@AricDiLalla) August 1, 2026 Mims is an All-Pro returner who can take it for a touchdown whenever he has the ball in his hands, but his work as a wide receiver has been inconsistent. He has yet to put together a full season of consistent production as a pass catcher; however, he has come up clutch for the Broncos in key moments, been a reliable deep threat, and had stretches of really good football. Could he finally be putting it all together? As we know, Mims is in a contract year, and we have seen players around the league have big years right before they head into free agency. If Mims can continue this sort of play throughout camp and into the regular season, he seems like a strong candidate to have a breakout season. JK Dobbins promises to stay healthy One of the big question marks surrounding this Denver Broncos team is the health and availability of veteran running back JK Dobbins. Throughout his NFL career, he has been unlucky and dealt with multiple serious lower body injuries. He has had an ACL and Achilles injury and suffered a season-ending Lisfranc injury last season. Now, he is back with the Broncos and is promising to stay healthy this season. J.K. Dobbins pinky promised the media he won't get hurt this year 😳 "Remember this day" pic.twitter.com/4DezK5PVPV — DNVR Broncos (@DNVR_Broncos) July 31, 2026 Dobbins told reporters that he promises to play in all 17 games this season and wants to lead the NFL in rushing. Before his injury last…

title: Sean Payton impressed with Malcolm Roach
summary: The Denver Broncos improved this offseason with their acquisitions via trade, free agency, and the 2026 NFL Draft. Continuity was a big theme for the franchise, who boast the most returning starter snap share in the league. However, they lost one significant contributor on the defensive side of the ball when John Franklin-Myers signed a […]
full_text: ENGLEWOOD, COLORADO - AUGUST 1: Malcolm Roach #97 of the Denver Broncos participates in training camp at Broncos Park Powered by CommonSpirit on August 1, 2026 in Englewood, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos improved this offseason with their acquisitions via trade, free agency, and the 2026 NFL Draft. Continuity was a big theme for the franchise, who boast the most returning starter snap share in the league. However, they lost one significant contributor on the defensive side of the ball when John Franklin-Myers signed a lucrative free agent contract with the Tennessee Titans. Over the past few drafts, the Broncos have drafted a pair of defensive linemen, Sai’vion Jones and Tyler Onyedim, who will hopefully develop into starting caliber players. They have all the traits and talent to do so. In the meantime, Denver will be banking on some of their more seasoned players on the frontlines to keep their defense performing at a high level in 2026. One of those is veteran defensive lineman Malcolm Roach. Roach signed with the Broncos back in March of 2024. Since then, he has been an important part of Denver’s rotation up front. Despite missing five games due to injury, the former Longhorns standout put together arguably his most productive season as a pro in 2025. Yesterday after practice, Head Coach Sean Payton lauded the seventh-year pro and stressed how important he is to the team’s defense. “He’s got a lot of juice. He’s one of those compound multipliers. A lot of his traits it’s infectious. I’ve said that about J.K. Dobbins—you hear him before you see him. They practice hard. I think all the way back to when he was undrafted out of Texas and we signed him, the improvement at his position for him has been remarkable,” stated Payton who pined for General Manager Mickey Loomis to sign him as an undrafted rookie free agent in 2020 with the New Orleans Saints. While most players get extensions after or before a season, Roach’s is an exception. His on the field prowess was a big reason the front office rewarded him with a three-year contract extension last November, right before Thanksgiving. The extension, worth over $28 million with half of it being guaranteed, shows the Broncos believe he will be crucial to their success this season and beyond. Prior to going down with injury, Roach was third in the Broncos’ defensive line snap share after Franklin-Myers and Zach Allen in their rotation. He finished the ‘25 season with 401 snaps, 41 tackles, 4 sacks, and 5 quarterback hits. Had he not missed five games, those numbers would have certainly been much higher. With over 500 snaps up for grabs due Franklin-Myers’ departure, the team will need Roach to step up and play his best ball to date. By all accounts, it seems that Roach is poised to be one of the first in line to make up for that. He has a big personality but also possesses the grit and determination to take his game to the next level. “He’s always going to be looking at what he can do a little better, how he can play on third down relative to the rush. He’s got really good football I.Q. and I think that it kind of shows up on film even at the defensive tackle position.”
author: Christopher Hart

title: Jaylen Waddle earning high praise from teammates at training camp
summary: Falling short of their ultimate goal last season, the Denver Broncos knew they had to make a big move to improve their shots at a Super Bowl title in 2026. This past march, the Broncos swung a gargantuan trade to add an explosive playmaker to their offense. Sending off a first and third round pick […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - JUNE 4: Jaylen Waddle (17) of the Denver Broncos speaks to members of the media during OTAs at the Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Thursday, June 4, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Falling short of their ultimate goal last season, the Denver Broncos knew they had to make a big move to improve their shots at a Super Bowl title in 2026. This past march, the Broncos swung a gargantuan trade to add an explosive playmaker to their offense. Sending off a first and third round pick [along with a fourth-round pick swap], Denver reeled in high-profile wide receiver Jaylen Waddle from the Miami Dolphins. It was an all-in move that was emblematic the team’s aggressiveness during the Sean Payton era. While the defense ranked among the NFL’s best in 2025, the offense posted league-average marks across the board. Waddle’s addition will certainly bolster the team’s offensive efficiency and productivity for their upcoming gridiron campaign. The cost was significant, but the franchise is confident the savvy wideout will give them some much needed juice on offense. Waddle has been a highlight reel thus far in camp. His speed and playmaking making ability have earned him significant praise from both coaches and players. Safety Brandon Jones, who spent three seasons alongside Waddle in Miami, spoke highly of his teammate after yesterday’s practice. “He’s exactly who he was in Miami. Might be a little faster, which is insane. I didn’t think that was physically possible, but great teammate, great person. He just brings a different type of juice,” stated Jones. “It’s a guy that can align anywhere, can catch any ball, run any route. Talks a lot of smack, too, which I appreciate. You kind of need that, especially during a training camp setting. Great dude, great teammate.” Waddle’s addition to the receiving corps gives them a strong five deep at the position. The leader of the room, Courtland Sutton, will also play a significant role in the Broncos’ aerial attack. Behind them, a slate of younger players is hoping to make an impact this season: Marvin Mims Jr., Troy Franklin, and second-year wideout Pat Bryant. While there are only so many targets to go around, Jones felt confident Waddle’s presence will give the aforementioned a chance to shine this season when the time comes. “I think it gives a lot of the other guys some opportunities depending on obviously down and distance and stuff like that,” added Waddle. Perhaps nobody in Denver is more excited about Waddle than Bo Nix. Entering his third season leading the Broncos on offense, Nix is looking to make the next jump as a quarterback. Through two seasons, Nix has proven he was worth his draft slot and then some. Nevertheless, there are certain aspects of his game that need a bit of work. With Waddle in the lineup, game day endeavors for Nix should be a little bit easier. In turn, those areas that need improvement will get better. After practice yesterday, he spoke happily and confidently about what Waddle can do to unleash their offensive potential. “He’s an explosive playmaker. The guy is really good at what he does. He makes plays, he’s fast, he’s really explosive. He’s great ball in hand, he’s great going to get the ball deep, he’s great in the screen game. He can do just a lot of things. He’s very versatile. He adds an extra element to our offense, and it’s exciting,” remarked Nix. “Middle of the field, outside, vertically, behind the line of scrimmage. Anywhere. We’re going to utilize him and whatever the defense is giving us, we’re going to attack.” The Broncos haven’t had a wide receiver duo that posted 1,000 yards since Demaryius Thomas and Emmanuel Sanders in 2016. This season, Sutton and Waddle have the chance to be the franchise’s most dynamic duo at the position in a decade. If all goes as planned, Waddle’s addition to the team will catapult Denver’s standing as a middle-of-the-road offense to one of the league’s best in ‘26.

title: Denver Broncos roster review: Tight end Adam Trautman
summary: Adam Trautman is another Sean Payton guy. He was drafted by the Saints in 2020 and headed to Denver in 2023. He’s a reliable tight end who can do a little bit of everything that the position requires. He’s been talked about mostly as a blocking tight end. That being said, he’s a guy who […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - DECEMBER 25: Adam Trautman #82 of the Denver Broncos exits the field at halftime during an NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Adam Trautman is another Sean Payton guy. He was drafted by the Saints in 2020 and headed to Denver in 2023. He’s a reliable tight end who can do a little bit of everything that the position requires. He’s been talked about mostly as a blocking tight end. That being said, he’s a guy who caught the ball when needed as a reliable target for Nix in the past couple of years, which is the reason the team signed him to an extension this offseason. Player Profile Adam Trautman | Tight End | Denver Broncos Height: 6′ 5″ Weight: 253 pounds Age: 29 years old Experience: 7th season College: Dayton 2025 stats: 20 catches for 195 yards, 1 TD Contract 2026 outlook with the Broncos Trautman is the one guy in the tight end room that has no question marks around him over the next two seasons at least. He’s a team player, knows the playbook in and out, is a willing run blocker, and can catch down the seam or on the sideline in a pinch. He’s got the history of run blocking under his belt, but seems fairly average to me at the actual job. I tend to think that is because he’s developed into a reliable pass catcher to round out what he does. This offense doesn’t need a true road-grading 285lb tight end to keep the run game moving. It does need a guy like Trautman who can do either aspect of the job at an average or above-average level at times so that they can stay on schedule or extend drives. Trautman may not be the flashiest of tight ends, but he’s the kind of reliable starter every NFL coach wants in the room. Final Word The biggest value I see in him on the team is as a veteran resource that is going to help the tight end room develop talent. Young players like Caleb Logner, Justin Joly, and Dallen Bently will be able to learn from him as the season wears on and have an excellent example of how to go about the business of being a professional tight end in this league. That’s not to say I don’t think he’s a good player. He is. He’s not the high-ceiling tight end this roster is yearning for (and has been for years, honestly). He wasn’t paid like that because both he and the Broncos know what his fit is on this team.

title: Broncos target 2027 groundbreaking for new stadium
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! Look for the Denver Broncos to break ground on their new stadium in 2027. At least that’s according to Broncos president Damani Leech after meeting with the media on Saturday prior to training camp practice. That would allow the franchise to meet its goal of completion in four years. Leech said […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - JUNE 18 : Burnham Yard photographed in Denver, Colorado on Thursday, June 18, 2026. (Photo by Hyoung Chang/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Look for the Denver Broncos to break ground on their new stadium in 2027. At least that’s according to Broncos president Damani Leech after meeting with the media on Saturday prior to training camp practice. That would allow the franchise to meet its goal of completion in four years. Leech said the groundbreaking goal is late spring or early summer of next year. The common theme remains now as it has throughout the process: The Broncos are taking a thoughtful approach and not rushing anything. “We feel like 2031 is still achievable for sure,” Leech said to the media. “Again, everybody has to be involved. Certainly, there’s things that we have to do and deliver to city council, but there’s other groups that are participating in the process in order to make that happen and make it a reality, but we think it’s realistic and achievable.” The Broncos are “laser focused” on opening their new stadium at Burnham Yard in 2031, per Damani Leech. Believes it’s still a realistic timeline. Burnham Yard is still the “preferred site” pic.twitter.com/S3k2YqlleJ — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 1, 2026 For now, Burnham Yard remains the “ preferred site ,” as it has for about a year. For Burnham to just be the site, Leech said, it’s beyond the Broncos’ control. In May, the franchise made a major step with the purchase agreement for Burnham Yard. “Ultimately, it goes to, when does city council approve all of those things?” he said on Saturday. “So you have to have a community benefits agreement signed, take that to city council, they approve our development agreement, they approve our rezoning agreement. There’s a number of agreements that have to be approved by city council. “If we move forward with DURA and tax increment financing, all of those things have to be approved by city council. Ideally, those would be approved right around the same time, and once that happens, I think that’s a good indicator we’ve moved off a preferred site.” In the meantime, the franchise has chosen an architect for the new stadium. If the new headquarters are an indication, the stadium will be a masterpiece. “We’ve been working with Manica, a global, world-renowned architecture firm, for a number of months now, and continue to progress on designs of the stadium,” Leech said. “I think the things that we’ve seen have been pretty beautiful. Greg and Carrie are very, very involved, have a great relationship with David and his team, and things are going well there. “Our master plan continues to iterate and evolve. Sasaki (an architecture, planning, landscape, and design firm) got us to a really great point. We’ve brought on Tryba Architects, which is a local Denver-based firm that’s done a lot of great work here in Denver to help us continue to evolve that master plan. “We look forward to sharing updated renders of that here in the very near future and stadium renders, when it’s ready, will be shared probably on a much longer-term timeline, but (I) look forward to sharing in the very near future some updated renders of the district and neighborhood master plan.” For those curious, yes, it appears the Broncos will go with the PSL route for the new stadium. That’s a private seat license, or fee, that gives you the right to purchase season tickets. “As you know, I think every stadium in the last 10-plus years that’s been built, there have been PSLs issued,” Leech said. “So it seems like it’s a pretty likely thing to happen, but we haven’t made any formal decisions on that.” Ultimately, the goal of the new stadium is to host the Super Bowl. “It’s certainly something that’s on our minds,” Leech said. “It’s on the mayor’s mind, the governor’s mind, I think, fans as well. I wouldn’t say it’s a thing that we think about every day. We do understand that the league is pretty prescriptive about how they award those well into the future, so it’s definitely something worth thinking about. Obviously, we’ve got to get into the stadium and operate it for at least a couple of years before we can play a Super Bowl, but I would love to host the Super Bowl.”

full_text: Detroit Lions defensive end Derrick Moore (9) walks off the field after practice during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, July 30, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Dan Campbell was back in front of the podium on Monday prior to the Detroit Lions’ fifth day of training camp, and that meant a bunch of injury updates that have been lingering for a few days. That said, the Lions coach made sure to reiterate that it’s not a season-ending injury for Detroit’s fourth-round pick. “It’s a little unfortunate, but at the same time, it’s not a season-ender,” Campbell said. “So that’s good news.” TE Miles Kitselman The Lions undrafted rookie tight end left Sunday’s practice with a leg injury and will also be out “a while.” For someone already on the roster bubble, this is a tough blow to his first season.

title: 9 standouts from Day 4 of Detroit Lions training camp
summary: After an off day on Saturday, the Lions returned to the practice field Sunday for their first training camp session in front of fans. Despite a threatening forecast, the rain held off, allowing Detroit to put together a lengthy, fast-paced, and competitive practice in shells. The defense set the tone on the final day before […]
full_text: ALLEN PARK, MICHIGAN - JULY 29: Malcolm Rodriguez #44 of the Detroit Lions looks on during Detroit Lions Training Camp at Detroit Lions Meijer Performance Center on July 29, 2026 in Allen Park, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images After an off day on Saturday, the Lions returned to the practice field Sunday for their first training camp session in front of fans. Despite a threatening forecast, the rain held off, allowing Detroit to put together a lengthy, fast-paced, and competitive practice in shells. The defense set the tone on the final day before the pads come on, turning in one of its strongest practices of camp while several players continued making their case for larger roles and roster spots. Below are my nine biggest standouts from the day. Keep in mind that the Lions held two individual competition periods, where I primarily observed the offensive and defensive line one-on-one pass-rush drills alongside Erik Schlitt. When necessary, I’ve also incorporated additional observations from Jeremy Reisman on the one-on-one coverage and seven-on-seven periods. Offensive line depth — Miles Frazier & Larry Borom With Blake Miller limited to individual drills, Penei Sewell receiving periodic rest, and Christian Mahogany still working his way back up to speed with the second team, Sunday served as another reminder of just how important quality depth and versatility are along the offensive line. Miles Frazier went from working almost exclusively at left guard early in camp to taking reps at left tackle, left guard, right guard, and right tackle during Sunday’s practice. It was a nonstop exercise in recalibrating his footwork and technique, yet he rarely looked out of place. Frazier appeared promisingly comfortable at tackle, even rotating in with the first team at right tackle while Larry Borom handled the sixth offensive lineman role. He also turned in one of the more impressive performances during one-on-one pass rush drills going 7-1 in a team-high eight reps. On one red-zone rep, after taking second-team reps at right tackle, Frazier immediately rotated in with the third team at right guard and snow-plowed Aidan Keanaaina out of the gap. His endurance and stamina stood out throughout the afternoon while further reinforcing his value as a versatile reserve and likely the team’s fourth tackle option. Borom continued to show why the Lions value him, seamlessly rotating between left tackle, right tackle, and the sixth offensive lineman role. He also finished a perfect 4-0 during one-on-one pass rush drills. Both players served as another reminder that Detroit has built enough depth and versatility to keep the offensive line from becoming a liability as the season progresses. Linebackers — Malcolm Rodriguez & Joe Bachie Malcolm Rodriguez continued to receive an abundance of work with the first-team defense at WILL linebacker, including a handful of red zone nickel reps, while also mixing in with the second team at MIKE linebacker. He was particularly sharp in coverage, highlighted by a step-for-step pass breakup against Sam LaPorta on a fourth-down goal-line corner route. Rodriguez also flashed against the run, recording a tackle for loss on an Isaiah Pacheco run off the right side. Overall, he looks noticeably more comfortable and decisive than the rusty version returning from injury last season. Joe Bachie followed suit with an impressive string of red-zone and goal-line reps that showcased why the coaching staff might be starting to trust the veteran. Rotating in for Rodriguez as the second-team MIKE linebacker during the first red-zone series, Bachie helped stonewall the run after Christian Izien had already blown up the previous play for a tackle for loss. Then came the goal-line period. On three consecutive plays, Bachie recorded a tackle for loss on first-and-goal, blanketed a tight end on a quick post route without drawing a target on second down, and finished the series by breaking up a Luke Altmeyer pass on third down. A Bachie barrage like that, after already starting to quietly put together a strong camp and, if Jimmy Rolder misses time, could have the inside track for the sixth linebacker spot. Defensive line depth – Ahmed Hassanein & Levi Onwuzurike The arrow continues pointing up for a bulked-up Ahmed Hassanein. His energy and trademark war cries echoing throughout practice remain impossible to miss. More importantly, the production is beginning to match the enthusiasm. Hassanein crashed down the backside to disrupt a run near the goal line, was the first defender to surge through on the lone kickoff during the end-of-game scenario with the first-team units, and later generated a pressure during that final four-minute drill. Lined up next to Alim McNeill, Hassanein looped inside on a stunt, with McNeill crashing in front, and beat Cade Mays cleanly, and forced a pressure, although Jared Goff answered with a strike to Jameson Williams. His versatility continues to stand out, and he looks increasingly capable of providing interior pass-rush juice while contributing on special teams. While Levi Onwuzurike is still working behind Tyler Lacy at big end and seeing most of his snaps with the second-team defense, it’s encouraging to see him beginning to rev his engine. During one-on-one pass rush drills, Onwuzurike gave Juice Scruggs the business with a powerful bull rush before following it up with a physical rep against Tate Ratledge. He carried that momentum into team drills,where he had an overwhelming pressure inside to force Teddy Bridgewater to dirt a ball. Later, during red-zone work, Onwuzurike crossed Miles Frazier’s face and quickly penetrated into Luke Altmeyer’s lap, forcing a hurried throw that nearly resulted in an interception. If Detroit’s defensive front is going to take another step forward this season, reclaiming the disruptive version of Onwuzurike will be a significant piece of that equation. Cornerbacks — Rock Ya-Sin & Keith Abney II Before practice, defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard expressed confidence in his secondary, emphasizing the value of having cerebral veterans in the defensive backfield. “The quarterbacks in this league are too good now. So, it’s all about lying to them,” Sheppard said. “You have got to be liars on defense. You have got a lot of that guy with the green dot on offense. Pre-snap, he has to see something and then post-snap, that picture has to change or else you’re sitting duck. And, these guys have done these things. They understand the why behind it.” Rock Ya-Sin backed up those comments with another encouraging day as he continued battling for a starting role. During one-on-one and seven-on-seven periods, Jeremy Reisman shared that Ya-Sin was fantastic against Isaac TeSlaa, forcing two incompletions in his pair of reps against the second-year wide receiver. He carried that momentum into full-team red-zone drills, opening the period by breaking up a pass intended for TeSlaa on a post in the end zone that Jared Goff launched up to TeSlaa from roughly the 20-yard line. A few plays later, Goff went back to TeSlaa on a fade near the goal line, Ya-Sin once again broke up the pass as it was reaching TeSlaa’s massive catch radius. The veteran cornerback consistently outmatched TeSlaa’s size and physicality throughout practice, refusing to give ground. Keith Abney II also had an encouraging afternoon. Still working primarily with the third-team defense, Abney nearly came away with two interceptions in the red zone. First, he dove in front of a seam route intended for Tarik Black in the end zone before nearly jumping a goal-line slant on fourth down while aligned at outside cornerback. For a rookie starting to find his footing, getting his hands on the football twice in high-leverage situations was another promising step in his development. Tight end — Anthony Firkser The Lions’ decision to bring Anthony Firkser back for a third stint with the organization already looks…
