title: Jadeveon Clowney won’t be reuniting with the Seattle Seahawks
summary: There’s a reunion coming for veteran edge rusher Jadeveon Clowney, but it’s not with the Seattle Seahawks. Clowney, who generated reported interest from the Seahawks earlier this offseason, is set for a return to the Houston Texans, the team that drafted him way No. 1 overall back in 2014. According to Houston Texans reporter and […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - DECEMBER 02: Kirk Cousins #8 of the Minnesota Vikings throws the ball while being pressured by Jadeveon Clowney #90 of the Seattle Seahawks in the third quarterduring their game at CenturyLink Field on December 02, 2019 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Abbie Parr/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s a reunion coming for veteran edge rusher Jadeveon Clowney, but it’s not with the Seattle Seahawks. Clowney, who generated reported interest from the Seahawks earlier this offseason , is set for a return to the Houston Texans, the team that drafted him way No. 1 overall back in 2014. According to Houston Texans reporter and NFL insider Aaron Wilson , Clowney’s deal is one year “with a maximum value of $8 million and a base value of $5.5 million.” “It’s great,” Clowney said after the signing. “It was a family decision. It wasn’t about the money. It was about legacy and chasing a Super Bowl. I’ve got a lot of game left and I want to contribute.” Clowney still lives in the Houston area so he gets to stayhome. He’d visited with the Cleveland Browns, another one of his former teams, before ultimately deciding to sign with the Texans. Clowney was famously traded to the Seahawks before the start of the 2019 regular season, playing out his contract year before joining the Tennessee Titans in 2020. His best statistical year came with Mike Macdonald and the Baltimore Ravens in 2023, which would’ve made a return to Seattle that much more intriguing. Houston’s defense was right up there with Seattle’s as one of the NFL’s best, and the 33-year-old Clowney will get to play alongside arguably the best edge rushing pair in the league: Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter. Houston has a Super Bowl caliber defense, but it needs a lot more from C.J. Stroud and a reworked Texans offense to finally get over the hump and even reach a Conference Championship for the first time. At $5.5 million, Clowney’s base salary is more than double what the Seahawks gave Dante Fowler Jr to more or less replace Boye Mafe. Not that it’s exorbitant money, but it’s a sign that the Seahawks were probably never really in the mix for Clowney once they landed Fowler. ( H/T Mainlander over on The Feed )

(Photo by Summer Lamont/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Across the NFL teams have reported for training camp and are preparing to make a run at the Lombardi Trophy during the 2026 season. That means fans are getting excited, not just about the players added through free agency and the draft during the offseason, but for players drafted in prior seasons who have yet to live up to the potential fans had hoped for at the time the player was selected. For the New Orleans Saints, one of those players the team had hoped to see more from is 2024 second round pick of the New England Patriots, Ja’Lynn Polk. Polk caught just 12 passes on 33 targets for 87 yards and a pair of touchdowns as a rookie for Jerod Mayo’s 2024 squad in New England, and then missed the entire 2025 season following shoulder surgery. While on injured reserve the Patriots traded Polk to the New Orleans Saints in a day-three pick swap, and now not only is Polk’s 2026 campaign over, his career appears over as well. According to reports, the 24-year old receiver has opted to retire from the NFL and has been placed on the reserve/retired list by the Saints. #Saints WR Ja'Lynn Polk , a 2nd round pick of the #Patriots in 2024, has retired from the NFL at age 24. pic.twitter.com/JCpnQVCyJT — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) August 2, 2026 Polk scored his first career touchdown against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 2 of the 2024 season, and then set career highs in receptions (3) and yards (30) against the San Francisco 49ers two weeks later. He retires as the least productive receiver drafted in the second round since practice time limitations were put into place in 2011 collective bargaining agreement. His 87 career yards are easily bested by the 228 receiving yards of the second least productive second receiver drafted since 2011, Dee Eskridge.

summary: 49ers sign RB Khalil Herbert and former Colts 6th-round edge rusher; waive Eli Apple“Herbert played sparingly in 2025 with the Jets. The 28-year-old was once viewed as a promising, big-play threat. He entered the NFL with 4.48 speed, but injuries have since zapped some of that explosive ability. Herbert will likely spell Kaelon Black and […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - SEPTEMBER 11: Talanoa Hufanga #29 of the San Francisco 49ers tackles Khalil Herbert #24 of the Chicago Bears during the game at Soldier Field on September 11, 2022 in Chicago, Illinois. The Bears defeated the 49ers 19-10. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images 49ers sign RB Khalil Herbert and former Colts 6th-round edge rusher; waive Eli Apple “Herbert played sparingly in 2025 with the Jets. The 28-year-old was once viewed as a promising, big-play threat. He entered the NFL with 4.48 speed, but injuries have since zapped some of that explosive ability. Herbert will likely spell Kaelon Black and Patrick Taylor in the preseason, assuming we don’t see much of Christian McCaffrey. ” This week, Herbert referred to his vision as a running back as “God’s gift.” It’s how he explains his ability to find running lanes and more on the field. The Bears have enhanced it. “We work on those things throughout the week, too,” Herbert said. “(Running backs coach David Walker) says, ‘A lot of people say you can’t teach vision.’ But he works on it to help us get our eyes right in the right place and help the O-line put them in a place to succeed.” ….His ability to identify landmarks on the defense, plant his foot and get upfield are part of that. Getsy describes Herbert as having a “cool patience about him.” “That’s as much as anything,” Getsy said. “I think Coach ‘Walk’ does a great job with those guys and training their eyes where they’re supposed to be. But I think Khalil’s got a really cool patience about him, that he’s able to kind of let things happen and make it feel like he’s not necessarily going full speed but he is, which then allows him to make cuts and read off the blocks of guys really well.” ….“When you start getting into rhythm, you start feeling the game more, feeling how the defense is playing, feeling how the O-line is blocking,” Herbert said. “And as that starts building up, you kind of just feel it. You’re able to feel how the game’s going and feel where there’s empty space once you get in rhythm.” Khalil Herbert and Virginia Tech found what they were looking for in each other (paywall) “When he did make weight, he lined up on the offensive line, later moving to defensive line and linebacker as he moved through middle school. It wasn’t until high school that his athleticism started to shine and the seeds of a future at running back were planted….. Like when he was younger, getting past those pudgier days, he works at it. [QB Hendon] Hooker, who is Herbert’s roommate, was heading in to watch film last weekend, as quarterbacks do, so the running back decided to join him. “His work ethic is just incredible,” Hooker said. “The way he can break down defenses while watching film and then implement it in the game is incredible.” “Those times kind of waiting and having to sit behind, I kind of learned a lot just about myself and about the game studying those guys and learning different moves, techniques, different things they do kind of helped me out, helped me to be where I am right now,” Herbert said. “So, everything works out in perfect timing, I think. This is just working out how everything’s supposed to work out.” That studiousness was forged by his parents, who stressed education and hard work throughout his life. Khari Sr. is an engineer who specializes in power generation and diesel mechanics. Khalil, who got a degree in business administration at Kansas, is pursuing a Masters of Information Technology at Virginia Tech. “He’s one of them types of people that when he gets serious about something, he’s all in,” Khari Sr. said. “He dissects and he studies, because he just always wants to be ahead of the game, more or less. But that’s with everything, not just football.” 49ers’ Dre Greenlaw details brutal road that included depression, 2 games in 614 days (paywall) “I don’t have to go out there and do more,” Greenlaw said. “I don’t have to go prove it to nobody. … I have to go play football still. But I don’t have to go out there and overdo and prove to them that I’m a football player, or who I am as a person. I think that’s going to help a lot.” Greenlaw tore his Achilles during the 49ers’ overtime Super Bowl loss to the Chiefs after the 2023 season. After a 10-month rehab, he played in two late-season games during the 2024 season before his quadriceps travails delayed his Denver debut last year to mid-October. “Going to Broncos, I’m thinking ‘This is the year I’m finally going to make it happen,’” he said. Greenlaw is confident this will be the year he finally makes it happen. It nearly has to be. He knows a third consecutive injury-plagued season could leave him with limited options in free agency in 2027, when he will turn 30. For now, Greenlaw said he has not felt this good physically since January 2024, when his Achilles began bothering him in the weeks before the Super Bowl. “It’s been one (injury) after another, one after another, and I’ve just been playing catch-up the whole time,” Greenlaw said. “But I just feel like I’m where I need to be now.” Report: 49ers work out veteran edge rusher Ogbo Okoronkwo “The veteran pass rusher has 17.5 sacks over his eight-year NFL career, including 7.5 sacks during his two seasons with the Browns. He recorded 4.5 sacks in 2023 and another three in 2024. His best season was in 2022 when he had five sacks with the Texans. Okoronkwo had no sacks last season, but only appeared in one game for the Eagles.” 49ers work out two more defensive players, including former Cardinals draft pick “Carter has spent time with the Minnesota Vikings, Las Vegas Raiders, and Washington Commanders. He originally entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent out of Army following the 2023 NFL Draft and has experience playing as an edge rusher. Thomas is a former Arizona Cardinals edge rusher who entered the NFL as a fifth-round draft pick out of Clemson in 2024. He spent his college career as a productive pass rusher and was viewed as an intriguing developmental prospect coming out of Clemson.”

They’ve also added Titus Leo, a 6’3″, 245-pounder who was drafted in the sixth round by the Colts in the 2023 NFL Draft. Leo has only appeared in four games during his tenure, most recently appearing on the Eagles’ practice squad in October 2025. We knew the 49ers were working out various defensive linemen. It was reported the team had a tryout with Ogbo Okonkwo, but ultimately went younger. Leo tested well at his Pro Day back in 2023, running a 4.69 40-yard dash, with a 129″ vertical jump — an elite number. To make room for both players, the 49ers waived cornerback Eli Apple and waived/injured Mikail Kamara after being carted off during Saturday’s practice. full_text: The San Francisco 49ers knew they couldn’t go another practice with only two healthy bodies at edge rusher. Keion White has an adductor injury . Rookie Romello Height sat out of Saturday’s practice with an undisclosed injury after being carted off with cramps last week , while Cameron Sample was sidelined with a knee injury. Oh, and undrafted free agent edge rusher Mikail Kamara was carted off with an apparent leg/knee injury. Already without the services of starting defensive ends Mykel Williams (active/PUP) and a recovering Nick Bosa, the 49ers worked out veteran edge rusher Ogbo Okoronkwo, a fifth-round draft pick out of Oklahoma back in 2018. The 31-year-old played one season in Los Angeles under Raheem Morris, when he was the defensive coordinator for the Rams. Since leaving the Rams in 2021, Okoronkwo spent a season playing under DeMeco Ryans with the Texans before spending the next two years with Jim Schwartz and the Browns. Okoronkwo was a part-time player for the majority of his career. He’s played roughly 400 snaps per season from 2022 through 2024. Last season, Okoronkwo was with the Eagles. His most productive season came in 2022 under Ryans, when Okoronkwo had an 18.5% pressure rate, 33 stops, and 5 sacks. We’ll see if Okoronkwo ends up being a player who ends up signing and contributing for the 49ers amid the injuries at the position, or ends up being nothing more than a veteran camp body.

title: The Golden Fool’s Mailbag: Mykel Williams/George Kittle return, 49ers injuries, Kyle Shanahan
summary: Remember these? We’re digging back into the mailbag to answer your questions. full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - APRIL 25: San Francisco 49ers international fan of the year David Roesler announces a pick during the third day of the 2026 NFL Draft at Acrisure Stadium on April 25, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Remember these? We’re digging back into the mailbag to answer your questions. The one answering them probably is the least insightful person on this site, but hey, we have fun doing it, right? So far, foot is in my mouth for De’Zhaun Stribling. I was very lukewarm on the pick initially and now I think he might be the guy for a long time. We need to see what he does when the other team is trying to take his head off, but so far I’ve read and seen nothing but good things. We’ll need it too, since the 49ers are down a wide receiver in Ricky Pearsall . Ok, now to the disclaimer. You want to see your question appear here? Then head on over to the feed when I post the ask and give me something to answer. I usually will make a call early in the week if I’m thinking about doing a mailbag. And yes, I know someone was asking me to cast the 49ers in the Odyssey . I have not seen the Nolan epic, though I studied it and the Iliad in college (was my favorite part actually). Given how passionate I am about that, I think a full post on it will be warranted. I just need to see the Nolan film first to get his take on it. If I’m going off just what I remember from the book, Kyle Shanahan would definitely be Odysseus. I have never seen BA and AB in the same place at the same time…coincidence…I think not Call Scully and Mulder and let’s get to the bottom of this -CanWeCloneJoe? Sorry, but Scully hasn’t been returning my calls. I guess she’s moved on. Though I have wondered, and will present the question to everyone: which has been more bizarre? Antonio Brown or Brandon Aiyuk? I still lean to Brown due to things like Mr. Big Chest, getting his feet frozen, and other theatrics, but Aiyuk is definitely fighting for that top spot. As far as the same place at the same time. Someone find a college game from Aiyuk where Brown is playing (maybe there was a Saturday game in December the two played?) That’s the best I can do. After all of the injuries, is it now the time to hire a Martial Arts trainer who specializes in injury prevention? Seb all the temporary (mostly) injuries seem to have taken our eyes off the prize if you will, when do you think we get Kittle and M Williams back? no_such_thing_as_nothing I’m not ready to say that just yet. You could be the Carolina Panthers that are losing multiple players for the season after the first week. The Ricky Pearsall news is devastating; I feel for the kid, but this has been going on since last year, and surgery was seen as the last resort. Yes, the 49ers have a lot of EDGE pieces sidelined right now, but most should be back. Yes, Stribling was out Saturday with tightness, but that happens to everyone at some point, especially rookies who don’t know what the rigors of training camp entail. I’d rather tightness put them in bubble wrap than have them work through it. Now, if the 49ers have another injury decimated season like last year—somethign has got to give. As far as George Kittle and Mykel Williams returning. Williams will be the first. He’s already doing high knees and the like as of yesterday . I’d expect him back later in August. For Kittle, he’s progressing, but I expect him to be activated a few weeks after the season starts. And for a martial arts trainer? I got just the guy, and it isn’t Mr. Miyagi . Maybe he can bring his buddy along . There is a lot of commotion around the Shanahan car crash and the fact that the team kept a lid on it and maybe also some of the local media did as well to curry favor with the team. Mike Florio, who is a certified toolshed (apologies to toolsheds everywhere, no harm intended) has gone as far as to compare the situation to the PR failure around the Vrabel/Russini situation. Can you explain why this is supposedly such a big deal? I get that Kyle is a public figure and the face of one of 32 NFL teams, but what difference does it make to have this reported immediately or not? CanWeCloneJoe? I’m pretty divided with this. On one hand, there was no foul play or anything like a mistress in the front seat. Just Shanahan grabbing his phone and hitting someone else. There’s nothing to report on besides a car crash. And after you hear about him losing a potential eye, my (very uninformed) guess is the 49ers got to play with California public records laws. Nothing indicates a cover-up beyond incorrectly identifying who was at fault. So why didn’t the 49ers just do what everyone else says and just say Shanahan was in a car wreck, and we’ll be updated when they feel we should be? Well, from what John Lynch said, it was more Shanahan’s decision, but the same question applies. The fan in me does not care about the wreck beyond the details of the incident itself, because there’s nothing within that is newsworthy for reasons I explained above. Now as to why it wasn’t reported? We can argue the semantics all we want. I’m not going to give opinions or guess on who was asked to withhold what, but the consensus is the Shanahan family wanted to go at their own pace . Given Shanahan had a concussion, he probably wasn’t in the right mind when thinking through this, but that seems to be how everything materialized. I understand why some people think someone dropped the ball on this, but I also think it was trying to keep all parties comfortable. For a public figure like Kyle Shanahan, that’s not exactly possible.

Stribling is big, accelerates out of cuts very smoothly, catches the ball cleanly, and seems to have quickly earned the trust of the quarterbacks. He’s been so good that Evans, a six-time Pro Bowler, all but shouted out his name on Friday when asked to name a standout young player. “Strib!” Evans said. “Strib’s standing out. He’s had a really good offseason and OTAs and he’s continued to do that in training camp.” I’m a zero-time Pro Bowler, but in my eyes, Stribling’s early-camp play has been more consequential than any 49ers highly drafted rookie receiver since Aiyuk in 2020 and Deebo in 2019 — and has already placed him above Pearsall, Dante Pettis, Danny Gray, and Jalen Hurd.” 49ers injuries: De’Zhaun Stribling has hamstring tightness; Keion White has an adductor issue “The more the top wideouts miss, the more other players will get their opportunities. We know about Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing, but undrafted free agent Wesley Grimes is a big beneficiary, as he could potentially slide into the “F” role, being a bigger body, as well as “Z” opposite Mike Evans.” 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris shares training camp updates “I’ve hated Deebo so long (laughter) and it’s so nice to have him back in a friendly atmosphere. He’s been one of those guys that’s been a highly competitive guy in the National Football League that you’ve got to deal with. No matter what the circumstance of the game is, what the situation is of the game, you’ve got to be aware. He’s the ultimate piece that can move around, and you have to game plan around him because of his ability to run the football, his ability to line up at receiver, his ability to take screens, his ability to do a bunch of different things on special teams, whether it be return man or whatever the case may be. He’s so versatile and we’ve used him so well in the Bay for so long. We were kind of catching up. Caught up yesterday, but it’s always good to see him, a face that’s familiar around this building and getting him back is really cool.” 49ers executive Paraag Marathe departing after 25 years to focus on soccer clubs “According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, executive vice president of football operations and president of 49ers Enterprises, Paraag Marathe, is leaving the 49ers to focus full-time on his leadership roles with Leeds United and Scottish club Rangers FC, as well as other sports ventures.” Deebo Samuel on reunion with 49ers: ‘Just matter of time’ “It kind of felt like I didn’t even go nowhere, to be honest,” Samuel said. “When I got back, I was just like, ‘Well, I know what’s going on. I know the people here. Staff still the same.’ So it’s kind of like the same for real.”

summary: The Tennessee Titans totally revamped their defensive line this offseason. They hired Robert Saleh to be the new head coach. Saleh came in and reimagined the defensive line in his vision. It started when the Titans traded for Jermaine Johnson II. They signed John Franklin-Myers, Jordan Elliott, and Jacob Martin in free agency. Mike Borgonzi […]
full_text: Tennessee Titans Coach Robert Saleh speaks before mandatory minicamp at Vanderbilt Health Football Center in Nashville, Tenn., Wednesday, June 17, 2026. | ANDREW NELLES / THE TENNESSEAN / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images The Tennessee Titans totally revamped their defensive line this offseason. They hired Robert Saleh to be the new head coach. Saleh came in and reimagined the defensive line in his vision. It started when the Titans traded for Jermaine Johnson II. They signed John Franklin-Myers , Jordan Elliott, and Jacob Martin in free agency. Mike Borgonzi also traded for Solomon Thomas. Saleh coached all five of these players in New York and San Francisco. Of course, they’re joining Jeffery Simmons, who inked a historic extension with the Titans earlier this offseason. Saleh will attempt to develop sophomore Femi Oladejo. The Titans also drafted Keldric Faulk with a first-round pick. Faulk was another Saleh-approved addition, given his similar length and build to Arik Armstead. The aforementioned eight players will essentially be the Titans’ defensive line rotation this season. Coach Saleh is expected to field an aggressive, attacking-style defense. That’s the focal point of his defense. It should lead to impressive sack numbers for the Titans’ defense. Expectations are high. Given the Titans’ lack of talent at EDGE last season, defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson actually did an excellent job manufacturing pressure. An All-Pro season from Simmons helped. The Titans ranked 12th (tied) in the league in sacks with 42. That exceeded preseason expectations. Interestingly enough, Saleh’s 49ers defense ranked last in the NFL in sacks with 20. Remember they lost Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams to season-ending ACL injuries. It’s a reminder that even the greatest defensive coaches need talented players to produce results. The Titans have an elite talent in Simmons, and Franklin-Myers should be very productive too. The EDGE spot is mysterious. Johnson is coming off a disappointing 2025 season and 2024 Achilles injury, and Oladejo disappointed as a rookie. Coach Saleh needs to elevate this defense to produce another 40+ sacks in 2026.

Commanders links Today’s sked: ⛅️: temps in mid to upper 70s; 🎤: Dan Quinn before practice 🏈: 8:30 am. 1st day in pads 🎤: Chig Okonkwo/Odafe Oweh after practice 👨🏻‍💻: camp nuggets to https://t.co/1YYxI4NQrS 🎥: video to https://t.co/1YYxI4NQrS 🗣️🎙️: podcast later today — John Keim (@john_keim) August 3, 2026 Articles Bleacher Report Most Important Contract Decision for Every NFL Team Ahead of 2026 Season Washington Commanders DT Daron Payne Commanders general manager Adam Peters said there’s no huge hurry to extend the 29-year-old after a down 2025. “I don’t think we’re gonna explore that at this time,” he said. “Really excited to have Daron with us next year, and can probably address that later, maybe after the year. But, and I’ve talked with his agent about that, what I can say is I got a ton of respect for Daron. His toughness, his physicality, his leadership, his ability to play and be available all the time. And there’s nobody tougher than him, and I think he’s going to really have a chance to flourish in this new defense, which will be a little bit multiple and allow him to move around a little bit.” It’s a decision that could come back to haunt the Commanders. The last time Payne was in a contract year, he exploded for a career-high 11 sacks. If that happens again, Peters is going to have a difficult choice to make, especially with multiple edge-rushers also set to hit the open market next spring. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) What CB Rasul Douglas brings to the Washington Commanders When the signing was first announced, I thought it was just a camp body to fill in while Amos recovered from his injury, but reports out of camp so far suggest Douglas has been one of the better corners on the roster in the opening few days of camp, having already recorded at least one interception and reportedly been close to quite a few more. Due to those positive reports, I thought I’d go back and watch some of his film from last year to see what he has to offer. He’s listed at 6-foot-2, 209 pounds and has long arms. With that size and length, you might think Douglas is a press-man corner. But actually he’s better suited to playing zone and match coverages, which fits what we’re expecting from new Commanders defensive coordinator Daronte Jones. When he’s playing off and with vision while keeping the play in front of him, he’s quick to react and close on receivers, where he can then use his length to get his hands in at the catch point and break up passes. Douglas also shows great instincts for coverage and awareness of game situations. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Roundtable Commanders add depth with signing of free agent center Julian Good-Jones, who served on the practice squad last season, was spotted taking reps with the ones as rookie Matt Gulbin rounded out the two-deep. Brandon Coleman is also entrenched in the starting competition at left guard, but he was also seen taking snaps at center following Saturday’s practice where he could become another candidate to reinforce depth while adding to his value to the unit. Yet Hill, 26, arrives back in the NFC where he will look to battle through training camp into the preseason. A former sixth round pick out of Georgia in the 2021 NFL Draft, Hill began his career with the Cincinnati Bengals where he started in three games and appeared in 24 through his first two seasons with the organization. He then fell out of the rotation after not appearing in any game during the 2023 season while being a healthy scratch in several games. Hill was then waived ahead of the 2024 season before joining Cincinnati’s practice squad. Hill then signed a reserve/futures contract with the Green Bay Packers in Jan. 2025 before being part of the final roster cuts, allowing him to land on the practice squad with the Chicago Bears exactly one month later. His most recent stint materialized with the Tennessee Titans after signing a reserve/future contract in January before being waived on June 16. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated 4 Things We’ll Learn From the Commanders’ First Padded Practice at Training Camp How the Offensive Line Holds Up Monday will give the team a chance to gauge whether its current options pass the sniff test presented by Washington’s defensive interior. The featured trench matchups to keep an eye on should be easily identified between Laremy Tunsil and Josh Conerly Jr against Odafe Oweh, K’Lavon Chaisson, Charles Omenihu, and Washington’s other edge rushers. The Commanders have a lot riding on Conerly’s ability to anchor against power and hold that edge from collapsing. They already know how he can move on the next level and as a mobile blocker, but they need to see how much raw power he added this offseason. The line has a lot to prove before anyone is going to fully trust Jayden Daniels behind what they have seen in the past. With the new system will come a new blocking structure. While we do not know the complete layout of that yet, it will likely be associated with the zone blocking scheme in some form, based on new OC David Blough’s lineage. Monday will also give the chance to see if the early camp dominance and pressure from the defense came mainly from the limitations you put on a group without contact in a contact-driven sport. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag Odafe Oweh is turning heads at training camp Oweh’s quickness has been easy to notice through the first week of training camp. He has reportedly generated multiple sack opportunities, something Washington is going to need to do a much better job of in 2026. The Commanders just didn’t make plays on defense last year. They only turned their opponents over 10 times, which ranked ahead of only the lowly interception-less New York Jets. Their 42 team sacks ranked slightly above league average, but they never seemed to come in defining situations. Five of the team’s projected starting front seven in the new 3-4 base unit — Oweh, K’Lavon Chaisson, Leo Chenal, Tim Settle Jr., and No. 7 overall pick Sonny Styles — are fresh faces, including both edge rushers and interior linebackers. Oweh has the scope to completely transform Washington’s defensive unit for the better. Styles will be the most important player on the Commanders’ defense in the long run , but it’s the former Baltimore Ravens and Los Angeles Chargers pass-rusher who needs to set the tone in the here and now. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag 5 standouts from Commanders 2026 training camp Day 4 Van Jefferson Jr. – Commanders WR Jefferson is a curious case. He looked well on course for a highly productive NFL journey during the early stages of his career with the Los Angeles Rams, but things tailed off dramatically. The Tennessee Titans also tasked him with too much last season , continuing his downward trend. It’s still early days, but things are looking up for Jefferson. If he keeps up this sort of consistency, the Commanders will have no choice but to take him through onto their 53-man roster. Rasul Douglas – Commanders CB Douglas has been among the standouts at training camp so far, and this continued during the first practice with fans in attendance. The Commanders are still without second-year corner Trey Amos, so Douglas is in a prominent role until further notice. He’s doing enough to keep it…

full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Ashburn, VA, USA; Washington Commanders wide receiver Jaden Bradley (86) participates in a drill on day one of training camp at BigBear.ai Performance Center at Commanders Park. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Former Washington Redskins 6th-round draft pick Colt Brennan was a star in college at the University of Hawaii and brought that hype with him to Washington in 2008. Brennan was a cult sensation during his brief time here, and was the inspiration for the annual Mason/Brennan Preseason Hype! Awards here at Hogs Haven. Brennan passed away at the way-too-young age of 37 five years ago . This was started as a tongue-in-cheek tribute to players that fans push to the moon before they play a snap, or after one great performance in the preseason. But it also puts the focus on some of the unheralded players who fans hype up and have a fighter’s chance at making Washington’s roster. Colt Brennan was a great college player that lit up the preseason, but injuries and other issues saw him flame out in the NFL early. RIP Colt and thanks for the inspiration. The Rules: 1. Player must have been drafted late or signed by the Redskins as an undrafted free agent. Players that have only been on other teams practice squads that are signed by the team are also eligible. 2. A player that has been on the team for several years is still eligible if most of that time has been spent on the practice squad, inactive, or with very limited productivity/time The Keenan “the Barbarian” Robinson Amendment: only 6th-round draft picks or later for their first two years in the league. This is the third year of the Adam Peters/Dan Quinn era in Washington, and they are looking for a big rebound from last year’s disappointing 5-12 season. They entered last season with Super Bowl aspirations after getting to the NFC Championship Game in Year 1. Quinn replaced both his coordinators, and Peters worked on fixing the broken defense. Training camp opened last week, so it’s time for another round of the Mason/Brennan Preseason Hype! Awards to check in on who’s getting fans excited early. title: Washington Commanders sign center Trey Hill
summary: Washington worked out multiple center prospects on Saturday, and today John Keim is reporting the team is signing one of them, center Trey Hill. Hill was drafted in the sixth round of the 2021 NFL draft by the Cincinnati Bengals. He played in twenty-five total games for the team, starting three, but was primarily a […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - JANUARY 02: Cincinnati Bengals center Trey Hill (63) warms up for the NFL football game between the Buffalo Bills and the Cincinnati Bengals on January 2, 2023, at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Michael Allio/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Washington worked out multiple center prospects on Saturday, and today John Keim is reporting the team is signing one of them, center Trey Hill. Hill was drafted in the sixth round of the 2021 NFL draft by the Cincinnati Bengals. He played in twenty-five total games for the team, starting three, but was primarily a backup and special teams contributor. The Commanders are Trey’s fifth team, with previous stops in Green Bay, Chicago, and Tennessee. At 6’4″ and 319 pounds, Hill is a big-bodied, physical center, and according to his draft profile, has a good anchor . He moves well for his size, but Hill appears to be a poor fit for an outside zone scheme. Trey will most likely provide another body at the center position for camp while Nick Allegretti recovers from a calf strain, but he does offer some guard versatility in a pinch. His best-case scenario might be as a replacement for Julian Good-Jones on the practice squad. In a corresponding move, the Washington Commanders released cornerback Tre Hawkins. Trey Hill 👀 pic.twitter.com/YlTMLhsFXc — Brandon Thorn (@BrandonThornNFL) August 30, 2021

title: Commanders early training camp observations: Who has stood out?
summary: Training camp has been very guarded through the first few practices. Media has been told not to film certain parts of practice or talk about certain alignments/plays. Just trying to figure out which inside linebacker spot Sonny Styles is playing, and who is running with the secondary’s first unit is hard. Since camp practices opened […]
full_text: Training camp has been very guarded through the first few practices. Media has been told not to film certain parts of practice or talk about certain alignments/plays. Just trying to figure out which inside linebacker spot Sonny Styles is playing, and who is running with the secondary’s first unit is hard. Since camp practices opened July 29, I have been taking as many notes as I can and have spoken to some people who have been in attendance to get their perspective. I have asked some situational questions, but the main thing I have been trying to glean before the pads come on Monday is this — who is standing out early on and for what reasons? Below are the players I’ve heard the most about through three practices. Commanders offense QB Jayden Daniels This is the guy everyone wants to hear about. Is the third-year quarterback under center more often? How many designed bootlegs is offensive coordinator David Blough running him on? Are his reads quick, accurate and decisive? Day 1 was a mixed bag, with the defense being significantly ahead of the offense (which is to be expected early on). From most reports, Jayden started off erratically but got better as the practice went on. Day 2 got better, with some really accurate passes in 7-on-7 and 11-on-11 red-zone work. The tempo of the offense was said to be a lot better and ball placement was excellent. Day 3, the first practice open to the fans, was easily his best day. David Harrison guesstimated he had around a 75% completion rate during team periods (with a few drops scattered in there as well). First glance at my notes, I charted Jayden Daniels at about 75% today with no interceptions between his 7-on-7 and 11-on-11 reps. — David Harrison (@DHarrison82) August 1, 2026 Jayden Daniels does a good job of knowing when to turn loose on a throw. Can throw with touch but also has a fastball. Saw that today — John Keim (@john_keim) August 1, 2026 WR Treylon Burks The big-bodied vet missed the second day of practice with a sore foot (precaution), but I’m hearing he’s been looking the part running with the first unit. Jayden mentioned him as a player who has stood out early on during camp, and we all saw the nice catch in the end zone he had over Amik Robertson with both feet in. He was the receiver who was mentioned as making the most plays during the first practice. Who will be WR2 for the Commanders? Jayden Daniels is looking for players he can trust. Daniels is happy with the WR room, and specifically mentioned Treylon Burks. pic.twitter.com/MgbnQF3BTZ — Marshall Kramsky (@marshallkramsky) August 1, 2026 5 ➡️ 13 pic.twitter.com/aZEZ84isD3 — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) July 29, 2026 WR Luke McCaffrey Luke McCaffrey’s name keeps being brought up from those who have attended practices. On Saturday, he was said to be the most targeted of the wide receivers during 7-on-7 and 11-on-11. Commanders WR Luke McCaffrey entering year 3 in Washington. Luke says you can tell the intent and detail in the David Blough offense. He also said Jayden has become more of a leader in the huddle. pic.twitter.com/rr1BhuL9er — Scott Abraham (@Scott7news) June 16, 2026 WR Antonio Williams Guys have been saying Antonio Williams continues to show the ability to win quickly off the jump. Commanders reporters mentioned him as a standout candidate during the 2-point conversion team period on the first day. He has also been getting some run with the first team and has been seen catching punts. When you get high praise from Terry McLaurin, you are doing something right. Terry McLaurin had some high praise for rookie Antonio Williams after today’s practice pic.twitter.com/QNYYxWqecH — Zach Selby (@ZachSelbyWC) July 30, 2026 TE Ben Sinnott A surprise, but not a surprise, Ben Sinnott has been showing out through the first three days of camp. The big-bodied, versatile tight end has been stacking good days and has caught the eye of many early on. In Saturday’s practice, he had an acrobatic catch on the sidelines during 2-minute drills that drew some applause from the crowd. That catch easily made up for an early drop. Sinnott also threw a bit of shade at Kliff Kingsbury (although probably not intentionally) for how he has been used in this new offense versus his previous two season in Washington. Ben Sinnott finally sees a path to revive his #Commanders ' fortunes under David Blough. ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/3M48wR3AoE — Riggo's Rag (@RiggosRag) August 1, 2026 TE Colston Yankoff On Day 2, Colston Yankoff had the catch of the day, going up between defenders to high-point a pass for a score. Reports had him just behind McCaffrey on Saturday with the most catches during team periods. Colson Yankoff who had a really nice TD catch Thursday going up and over defenders will get some extra chances to shine with John Bates missing time with a hammy injury pic.twitter.com/C90s4nCes8 — Mitchell Tischler (@Mitch_Tischler) August 1, 2026 Defense Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson Multiple people have commented on Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson wreaking havoc throughout the first three days of practice. Both have explosive first steps and supposedly they are giving Washington offensive tackles all they can handle. Mind you, there are no pads on yet, and this will usually favor defensive linemen when working against the offensive front five, but if the explosiveness is any indication of what we’ll see once pads come on, we all may be in for a treat this season! It sounds like he’s getting work at both MIKE and WILL and is someone who is in consideration for the green dot. Monday should tell us more when the pads are on for the first time this summer. Commanders links Articles WUSA9 Commanders training camp: Jayden Daniels turns 2025 injuries into gratitude In a WUSA9 one-on-one, Jayden Daniels said his injury-filled 2025 season taught him gratitude as he builds chemistry at Commanders training camp In some ways, it’s easy to lead a group of guys who genuinely want to be part of something bigger than themselves as individuals. But convincing them you’re the one worth following is the hard part. Jayden Daniels has a special relationship with Commanders Offensive Coordinator David Blough. Daniels thinks Blough is "brillant" pic.twitter.com/z8YSn3Jd1W — Marshall Kramsky (@marshallkramsky) August 1, 2026 One of the main reasons, if not ‘the’ main reason, tight end Chig Okonkwo chose to come to Washington as a free agent was for the opportunity to play with Daniels. The tight end is not a wide receiver by label, but his potential to have a major impact on the team’s passing game is well established to the point where he may become the team’s second receiver in a lot of ways. To that end, Daniels describes his new tight end as the type of player who “when the game’s on the line, (he’s) like, ‘Hey, 5, throw me the ball. You can trust me. I’ll go make a play.’” “You just want that dog mentality, not just from me and Terry or (left tackle Laremy Tunsil), other guys, but just from the whole offense.” Who will be WR2 for the Commanders? Jayden Daniels is looking for players he can trust. Daniels is happy with the WR room, and specifically mentioned Treylon Burks. pic.twitter.com/MgbnQF3BTZ — Marshall Kramsky (@marshallkramsky) August 1, 2026 As those of us outside the organization continue to search for evidence of a true No. 2 wide receiver, however, “I commend Treylon Burks for what he’s done and the stuff that he’s battled throughout his career to get to this point,” Daniels said. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Washington Post (paywall) Five takeaways from Week 1 of Commanders training camp Nickelback looks to be a rotational spot The Commanders focused on red-zone drills during team periods in practice this week, so the defense typically lined up in a base formation, but they still frequently mixed in their nickel package. While Mike Sainristil took most of the nickelback snaps, it’s clear he won’t be the only player to spend significant time there. Safeties Nick Cross and Quan Martin also rotated in as slot defenders. While using a bigger nickel can be detrimental in man coverage, it allows Washington to keep more run support and blitz ability on the field. The plan for the snap breakdown at nickelback will become clearer once Amos returns from injury. He’s expected to be a starter on the outside while Sainristil, Amik Robertson, Ahkello Witherspoon and Rasul Douglas are competing for the other spot. Sainristil, Robertson and Douglas have all spent time working from the slot, and they could take on larger workloads there if they don’t win the job on the outside. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Last Man Standig (paywall) Legends, injuries and big-man catches highlight Commanders camp practice: The Daily Install Better day for the receivers as well. Van Jefferson and Jaylin Lane were active pass catchers in 11-on-11 and 7-on-7 drills. I remain bullish on the sure-handed Jefferson’s opportunity, but he’ll have to show high rotation worthiness to make the 53. Dyami Brown and Marcus Mariota connected down the field . Kicker scoreboard: Jake Moody made all eight field-goal attempts from various distances. UDFA Drew Stevens finished 7 of 9, with misses from 45-48 yards. He also connected from 50-plus, as did Moody. Dan Quinn opened practice by having the offense run a play from the opponent’s 30 before sending out the field-goal unit. The attempts were all from 40-plus yards. Moody went 3 for 3. Stevens finished 2 for 3. During the standard six-kick session, Moody remained perfect while Stevens went 5 for 6. TE Lawrence Cager absolutely looks the part of an NFL tight end. With Bates sidelined, Cager used his extra reps to demonstrate his pass-catching ability. Whether he can beat out Yankoff for the TE4 spot remains one of the more interesting camp battles. For more from Ben Standig, click here Bullock’s Film Room (this story can be read in full free of charge) Rounding up and breaking down some clips from the first few days of Commanders training camp As you’ll likely know, I’m not a beat reporter and I live in Europe, so I’m not at these practices. If you’re looking for a report of everything going on at each practice, I suggest following the main beat reporters like Ben Standig, John Keim, Nicki Jhabvala and J.P Finlay, among others. All I can go off of is clips that get posted on social media. Unfortunately, the Commanders are annoying strict about what gets posted and shared online. So while teams like the Ravens are live streaming their training camp practices and seemingly every play from the Cardinals training camp gets posted online, Commanders fans get very little. But after the first few practices, I’ve finally found enough clips to put together a post that is hopefully worth reading. So here is a few breakdowns of some plays from Commanders training camp that I was able to find online. Another clip that stood out on the opening day came from Washington Informer reporter Skylar Nelson. A quick look at Antonio Williams from today’s training camp practice pic.twitter.com/L1ySGvDa3j — Skylar Nelson (@SkyMad03) July 29, 2026 Rookie receiver Antonio Williams lines up in the slot and runs what appears to be a choice out, otherwise known as a C.O. It’s a route that is designed to look like a choice route with the release and build up to the break, but the route is always designed to break outside, instead of having the actual choice to break inside or outside. Choice routes and the routes that work off of them are likely to be a significant part of this offense, so this rep is worth looking at in detail. I wrote after the draft how Williams could be in contention for the Amon-Ra St.Brown role in this offense . Being able to set up and execute choice routes and the group of routes in that tree is critical to playing that role effectively. Obviously it’d be great to see it against a defender rather than just on air, but you can see that the movement skills to run these types of routes are there. To read more of this 700-word article, CLICK HERE Commanders.com Training camp notebook | Treylon Burks returns to practice for ‘Back Together Saturday’ Jeremy McNichols continues to show that he can make plays, despite being on the older side for a running back. He had a pair of nice runs to the outside during team drills, beating a few defenders to the sideline for a decent gain. McNichols has managed to stick around because he runs hard and knows how to pick up third downs in the passing game. It’s still unclear what the depth chart is going to look like at the position, but McNichols is continuously proving why he needs to be part of the rotation. The receiver room is not perfect, but there have been moments where it’s easier to see why the Commanders like the options they have at the position. Burks has stood out at times with his size and ability to make contested catches; Daniels clearly trusts Dyami Brown and his abilities downfield; and Van Jefferson has managed to create separation with his route running ability. There’s always a chance for them to add…

title: How the Washington Commanders might utilize 12 and 13 personnel this season
summary: During the early days of training camp, ESPN reporter John Keim caught up with Ben Sinnott to discuss how offensive coordinator David Blough plans to utilize the Commanders tight ends this season. Clearly, Sinnott was excited about the possibilities in Washington’s new offense. Head coach Dan Quinn has also detailed to reporters the role they […]
full_text: During the early days of training camp, ESPN reporter John Keim caught up with Ben Sinnott to discuss how offensive coordinator David Blough plans to utilize the Commanders tight ends this season. Clearly, Sinnott was excited about the possibilities in Washington’s new offense. “It’s not even close,” Sinnott said. “So many different variations. Today we’re lining up at number one, we’re running five-step ins, we’re running corners, we’re running options, we’re running flat [routes]. We’re just doing everything. It’s so much fun. It’s a breath of fresh air for this offense and how it uses tight ends.” Head coach Dan Quinn has also detailed to reporters the role they see for free agent addition Chigoziem Okonkwo. “Long play-action passing, over routes, pylon routes, things that are down the field, crossing routes that are catch-and-run to use some of his speed,” Quinn said. Previously, we examined how much the Washington Commanders might run heavy personnel this season, but today we look at a couple of examples of what it might look like on the field. 12 Personnel Likely the personnel grouping most utilized by the Commanders offense this year, 12 personnel involves one running back, two tight ends, and two wide receivers. The team has emphasized the need for multi-dimensional running backs while adding Okonkwo as a big receiving threat. To gain an understanding of how Blough might use Chig out of 12 personnel, we take a look at an All-22 breakdown of Sam LaPorta with the Lions in 2023. Ben Johnson was Detroit’s offensive coordinator and then-Lions quarterback David Blough was on the practice squad that year. LaPorta showed promise when lined up as a WR in 2023, as well. This gave Ben Johnson and the Lions opportunities to use 12 Personnel groupings to create 11 Personnel formations. #Lions #DetroitLions pic.twitter.com/9wWqUCeRnh — All 22 Films (@All_22_NFL_Cuts) June 19, 2024 There is nothing too flashy about LaPorta’s deployment; Johnson essentially uses his size and agility in 11 personnel formations to create mismatches against cornerbacks and linebackers. Okonkwo has already been utilized as a receiving threat by the Titans last year, with 56 receptions on 79 targets for 560 receiving yards. However, according to Next Gen Stats , Okonkwo functioned primarily in the short area of the passing game, with 62 targets coming in the first 10 yards of the line of scrimmage. Blough will likely get him more work in different areas of the field as detailed by Quinn. After being named Chicago’s head coach, Johnson continued to use 12 personnel with the Bears in a decidedly run-heavy scheme. The Commanders offense is expected to do the same. Chicago Bears running Duo in 12 Personnel with an extra OL pic.twitter.com/zl5JJ8QgiA — Last of the Fullbacks (@TheLastFullback) November 5, 2025 13 Personnel We start our look at 13 personnel with a detailed breakdown of a play by The Athletic’s Ted Nguyen. He analyzes the Los Angeles Rams in 13 personnel on second down with four yards to go. Receiving tight end Terrance Ferguson is split out wide, and Davis Allen is the H-back, with Davante Adams on the opposite side. The defense loads up to stop the run, but Sean McVay calls a passing play out of the look. Allen goes into inside motion and when the ball is snapped, he runs a vertical sail route. Ferguson runs a deep fade, and Adams a deep dig. Nguyen explains how the coverage dictated by the defense playing the run allows Allen to clear the safety and provides space for the completion to Adams. Rams running 11 personnel pass plays with 13 personnel pic.twitter.com/eLoLdXptJV — Ted Nguyen (@FB_FilmAnalysis) August 1, 2026 For the Commanders, Okonkwo would be split outside with Sinnott in the H-back role and Bates in-line. The goal would be to create an opportunity for Terry McLaurin, but Okonkwo is a viable threat on the outside and Sinnott operates well in the seam and would also be one. A multidimensional running back in the backfield keeps the defense honest and adds additional ways to attack the defense. Here is another look at 13 personnel used by Ben Johnson and the Bears for a 2-point conversion in the NFC wild-card game last season. Chicago lines up in a 13 personnel look with Colston Loveland in-line on the left, Cole Kmet in-line on the right next to a third offensive tackle, and Durham Smythe at fullback. Before the snap, all three tight ends motion out, creating a spread formation as described here by Chicago Bears analyst Coach Usayd Koshul . The #Bears will be using more 13 personnel in 2026 and this 2-point conversion playcall from the Wild Card win against #Packers serves as an example of why Ben Johnson made such a push to draft Sam Roush. The most underrated part of this play is that Green Bay is expecting run,… pic.twitter.com/saqVdjCqxk — Coach Usayd Koshul (@usaydkoshul) May 4, 2026 The end result is Loveland one-on-one with a linebacker on the outside and an easy conversion. Again, you can see how Washington’s current personnel could fit the same play call, with Chigoziem in Loveland’s role, Bates in Kmet’s, and Sinnott shifting out from the fullback position. Blough might also opt to keep the formation the same and run the play as presented with a power back like Kaytron Allen running behind the heavy look. In order to run these personnel groupings, the team needs players that are versatile and effective in multiple roles. Currently, the Commanders have three such players in Okonkwo, Sinnott, and Bates and while they may be more specialized in one aspect or another, each can function in multiple roles. Roster depth will also be key, and with blocking specialist John Bates on the shelf with an injury , the team will give Colson Yankoff and Lawrence Cager extended looks. Yankoff saw additional time last year when Ertz went out for the season and ended up playing 12% of the team’s total offensive snaps, both in-line and at fullback. The converted quarterback had the catch of the day during Thursday’s session training camp session. Undrafted free agent Quentin Moore will also get a longer look while Bates is recovering. Their continued development will be something to monitor as training camp ramps up this week.
